-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m6p1t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS InstanceA, InstanceB, Instructions, LeaseSpan, ClockCap, NoEngine

Engines == InstanceA \cup InstanceB

Amount(i) == 2 * i + 1

RECURSIVE Total(_)
Total(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
            ELSE LET k == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                 IN Amount(k) + Total(S \ {k})

MaxSettled == Total(Instructions)
NoDraft    == [item |-> -1, base |-> -1]
DraftSpace == {NoDraft} \cup [item : Instructions, base : 0 .. MaxSettled]

VARIABLES ledger, posted, leaseOwner, leaseUntil, draft, clock
vars == <<ledger, posted, leaseOwner, leaseUntil, draft, clock>>

\* The ledger is owned by whichever engine holds an unexpired lease; the lease
\* lapses purely by clock advance, so an engine can be holding a draft it read
\* under a lease it no longer owns.
Holds(e) == leaseOwner = e /\ clock < leaseUntil

TypeOK ==
  /\ ledger \in 0 .. MaxSettled
  /\ posted \subseteq Instructions
  /\ leaseOwner \in Engines \cup {NoEngine}
  /\ leaseUntil \in 0 .. (ClockCap + LeaseSpan)
  /\ clock \in 0 .. ClockCap
  /\ draft \in [Engines -> DraftSpace]

Init ==
  /\ ledger = 0
  /\ posted = {}
  /\ leaseOwner = NoEngine
  /\ leaseUntil = 0
  /\ draft = [e \in Engines |-> NoDraft]
  /\ clock = 0

Grab(e) ==
  /\ clock >= leaseUntil
  /\ leaseOwner' = e
  /\ leaseUntil' = clock + LeaseSpan
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, posted, draft, clock>>

Stage(e, i) ==
  /\ Holds(e)
  /\ draft[e] = NoDraft
  /\ i \notin posted
  /\ \A f \in Engines : draft[f].item # i
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![e] = [item |-> i, base |-> ledger]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, posted, leaseOwner, leaseUntil, clock>>

Post(e) ==
  /\ Holds(e)
  /\ draft[e] # NoDraft
  /\ ledger' = draft[e].base + Amount(draft[e].item)
  /\ posted' = posted \cup {draft[e].item}
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![e] = NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseUntil, clock>>

Discard(e) ==
  /\ ~Holds(e)
  /\ draft[e] # NoDraft
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![e] = NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, posted, leaseOwner, leaseUntil, clock>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < ClockCap
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, posted, leaseOwner, leaseUntil, draft>>

GrabStep    == \E e \in Engines : Grab(e)
StageStep   == \E e \in Engines, i \in Instructions : Stage(e, i)
PostStep    == \E e \in Engines : Post(e)
DiscardStep == \E e \in Engines : Discard(e)

Next == GrabStep \/ StageStep \/ PostStep \/ DiscardStep \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(GrabStep) /\ WF_vars(StageStep)
        /\ WF_vars(PostStep) /\ WF_vars(DiscardStep)

\* No lost update: the balance must account for every amount ever posted, so a
\* write computed from a base read before another engine's write is excluded.
NoLostUpdate == ledger = Total(posted)

\* Progress: the shared pool of instructions drains completely.
EverySettled == <>(posted = Instructions)
========================================================================

CONSTANTS
  InstanceA = {a1}
  InstanceB = {b1}
  NoEngine = nil
  Instructions = {1, 2}
  LeaseSpan = 2
  ClockCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
PROPERTY EverySettled
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Two settlement engines run a bank's overnight interbank batch: one belongs to the primary site instance and one to the standby site instance, but the two instances are not partitioned -- they draw from a single shared pool of settlement instructions and write to a single shared ledger record. Write access to that ledger is granted by a lease with an expiry: an engine may take the lease only when the outstanding lease has already expired against the batch clock, and the lease it receives runs for a fixed span of clock ticks measured from the moment it was taken.

The full action set is: Grab -- an engine takes the ledger lease when the current lease has expired against the clock, stamping a fresh expiry a fixed span ahead of the current clock. Stage -- an engine that currently holds a live lease and is not already carrying a draft picks an instruction that has not been posted and that no other engine has drafted, and copies the current ledger balance into its draft as the base value it computed from. Post -- an engine whose lease is still live applies the draft it carries, writing the draft's recorded base plus the instruction's amount into the ledger and marking that instruction posted. Discard -- an engine whose lease has lapsed throws away the draft it was carrying, releasing that instruction back into the shared pool. Tick -- the batch clock advances by one, up to a fixed cap; clock advance is the only thing that causes a lease to lapse.

The hazard the lease is there to prevent is a lost update. An engine that read the ledger balance under its lease, and then lost the lease to the other instance's engine while the clock advanced, is still carrying a draft whose base is stale. If it were allowed to post that draft, its write would overwrite whatever the second engine had already written, and the amount that second engine settled would silently vanish from the ledger even though it is recorded as posted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The ledger balance always equals exactly the sum of the amounts of the instructions recorded as posted, so no already-posted settlement amount is ever overwritten and lost by a write computed from a stale base.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every settlement instruction in the shared pool is eventually posted to the ledger.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m8p4t4 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Shelves, Slots, Arms, NoArm, CapLo, CapHi, MaxDose

Bins == Shelves \X Slots

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
                 ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
                      IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES shelfLock, binLock, held, cap
vars == <<shelfLock, binLock, held, cap>>

\* A dispensing arm must take the coarse shelf lock before any fine bin lock on
\* that shelf, and must give the bin locks back before the shelf lock.
Load(s) == SumOver(held, {s} \X Slots)
BinsOf(s) == {s} \X Slots

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelfLock \in [Shelves -> Arms \cup {NoArm}]
  /\ binLock \in [Bins -> Arms \cup {NoArm}]
  /\ held \in [Bins -> 0 .. MaxDose]
  /\ cap \in [Shelves -> CapLo .. CapHi]

Init ==
  /\ shelfLock = [s \in Shelves |-> NoArm]
  /\ binLock = [b \in Bins |-> NoArm]
  /\ held = [b \in Bins |-> 0]
  /\ cap = [s \in Shelves |-> CapHi]

TakeShelf(a, s) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = NoArm
  /\ \A t \in Shelves : shelfLock[t] # a
  /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = a]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<binLock, held, cap>>

TakeBin(a, s, k) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = a
  /\ binLock[<<s, k>>] = NoArm
  /\ binLock' = [binLock EXCEPT ![<<s, k>>] = a]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, held, cap>>

Dispense(a, s, k, n) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = a
  /\ binLock[<<s, k>>] = a
  /\ held[<<s, k>>] + n <= MaxDose
  /\ Load(s) + n <= cap[s]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![<<s, k>>] = @ + n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, binLock, cap>>

ReleaseBin(a, s, k) ==
  /\ binLock[<<s, k>>] = a
  /\ binLock' = [binLock EXCEPT ![<<s, k>>] = NoArm]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, held, cap>>

ReleaseShelf(a, s) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = a
  /\ \A b \in BinsOf(s) : binLock[b] = NoArm
  /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoArm]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<binLock, held, cap>>

\* Retuning the shelf's ceiling is admission-controlled: a pharmacist may only
\* set a ceiling that still covers what is already sitting in the shelf's bins.
Retune(s, v) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = NoArm
  /\ v # cap[s]
  /\ v >= Load(s)
  /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![s] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, binLock, held>>

Collect(s, k) ==
  /\ binLock[<<s, k>>] = NoArm
  /\ held[<<s, k>>] > 0
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![<<s, k>>] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, binLock, cap>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Arms, s \in Shelves : TakeShelf(a, s) \/ ReleaseShelf(a, s)
  \/ \E a \in Arms, s \in Shelves, k \in Slots :
        TakeBin(a, s, k) \/ ReleaseBin(a, s, k)
  \/ \E a \in Arms, s \in Shelves, k \in Slots, n \in 1 .. MaxDose :
        Dispense(a, s, k, n)
  \/ \E s \in Shelves, v \in CapLo .. CapHi : Retune(s, v)
  \/ \E s \in Shelves, k \in Slots : Collect(s, k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The shelf ceiling is never overrun, neither by a dispense that ignores
\* headroom nor by a retune that drops the ceiling under standing stock.
WithinShelfCeiling == \A s \in Shelves : Load(s) <= cap[s]
=======================================================================
nl:
An automated pharmacy prescription dispenser is organised into shelves, and each shelf is divided into slots; a bin is one slot on one shelf. Two robotic dispensing arms move over the cabinet. To avoid tearing a shelf's contents apart, the arms follow a strict two-level locking discipline: an arm must take the coarse lock on a whole shelf before it may take the fine lock on any individual bin of that shelf, an arm may hold at most one shelf at a time, and it must hand every bin of that shelf back before it hands the shelf back. Each shelf also carries a stock ceiling that a pharmacist can change while the machine is running.

The full action set is: TakeShelf -- an arm takes the coarse lock on a free shelf, provided it is not already holding some other shelf. TakeBin -- an arm that already holds the coarse lock on a shelf takes the fine lock on one free bin of that shelf. Dispense -- an arm holding both the shelf lock and the bin lock adds a number of units into that bin, provided the bin has room for them and the shelf's current stock stays within the shelf's stock ceiling. ReleaseBin -- an arm gives back a fine bin lock it holds. ReleaseShelf -- an arm gives back the coarse shelf lock, but only once every bin of that shelf is unlocked, which enforces the release order. Retune -- a pharmacist changes a shelf's stock ceiling while no arm holds that shelf, and only to a value that still covers the stock already standing in that shelf's bins. Collect -- a patient picks up everything in an unlocked bin, emptying it and freeing shelf stock.

The interesting failure is not that two arms collide: it is that the shelf's stock ceiling is a moving target. Stock can be pushed up to the ceiling by a dispense, and the ceiling itself can be pulled down by a retune, so either side can be the one that overruns the shelf if it does not check the other.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every shelf, the total number of units standing across that shelf's bins never exceeds that shelf's currently configured stock ceiling, even though the ceiling can be changed while stock is standing.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m7p0t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, NoCar, MinLine, MaxLine

Stages == {"waiting", "online", "arming", "blasting", "done"}

VARIABLES reg, stage, seen, lineCap
vars == <<reg, stage, seen, lineCap>>

\* The high-pressure blaster is claimed through a compare-and-swap register: a
\* car first copies the register into its own view, then swaps itself in only if
\* the register still equals that view. A failed swap forces a fresh read.
OnLine == {c \in Cars : stage[c] \in {"online", "arming", "blasting"}}

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
  /\ stage \in [Cars -> Stages]
  /\ seen \in [Cars -> Cars \cup {NoCar}]
  /\ lineCap \in MinLine .. MaxLine

Init ==
  /\ reg = NoCar
  /\ stage = [c \in Cars |-> "waiting"]
  /\ seen = [c \in Cars |-> NoCar]
  /\ lineCap = MinLine

Admit(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "waiting"
  /\ Cardinality(OnLine) < lineCap
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "online"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, seen, lineCap>>

ReadReg(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "online"
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "arming"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, lineCap>>

SwapIn(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "arming"
  /\ seen[c] = NoCar
  /\ reg = NoCar
  /\ reg' = c
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "blasting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, lineCap>>

SwapFail(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "arming"
  /\ ~(seen[c] = NoCar /\ reg = NoCar)
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "online"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, seen, lineCap>>

Exit(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "blasting"
  /\ reg' = NoCar
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, lineCap>>

\* The conveyor operator re-rates the line while cars are on it, but never
\* below what is already rolling, so admitted cars are not stranded.
Relength(v) ==
  /\ v # lineCap
  /\ v >= Cardinality(OnLine)
  /\ lineCap' = v
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, stage, seen>>

AdmitStep    == \E c \in Cars : Admit(c)
ReadStep     == \E c \in Cars : ReadReg(c)
SwapStep     == \E c \in Cars : SwapIn(c)
FailStep     == \E c \in Cars : SwapFail(c)
ExitStep     == \E c \in Cars : Exit(c)
RelengthStep == \E v \in MinLine .. MaxLine : Relength(v)

Next == AdmitStep \/ ReadStep \/ SwapStep \/ FailStep \/ ExitStep \/ RelengthStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(AdmitStep) /\ WF_vars(ReadStep) /\ WF_vars(SwapStep)
        /\ WF_vars(FailStep) /\ WF_vars(ExitStep)

\* The register is an exact mirror of blaster occupancy: a car is under the
\* blaster iff the register names it. Since the register holds one value, this
\* leaves room for at most one car in the blast stage at any instant.
BlasterExclusive == \A c \in Cars : (stage[c] = "blasting") <=> (reg = c)

EveryCarWashed == <>(\A c \in Cars : stage[c] = "done")
==========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
  NoCar = clear
  MinLine = 1
  MaxLine = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BlasterExclusive
PROPERTY EveryCarWashed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line runs cars past a single high-pressure blaster. The blaster is the critical resource: exactly one car may be in the blast stage at a time, and the conveyor controller arbitrates it with a compare-and-swap register that names the current occupant, or reads clear when the blaster is empty. A car does not simply write itself into that register; it first copies the register into its own private view, and only then attempts the swap, which is accepted only if the register still holds the value the car copied. The number of cars allowed onto the line at once is a rating that the operator can change while the line is running.

The full action set is: Admit -- a waiting car rolls onto the line, provided the number of cars already rolling is under the current line rating. ReadReg -- a car on the line copies the current blaster register into its private view and moves to the arming stage. SwapIn -- an arming car swaps itself into the register and enters the blast stage, but only if its private view read clear and the register still reads clear, so a swap based on a view that has been overtaken cannot succeed. SwapFail -- an arming car whose view or whose register no longer reads clear abandons the attempt and drops back to re-read the register. Exit -- the car in the blast stage finishes, writes the register back to clear, and leaves the line finished. Relength -- the operator re-rates the line to a different length while cars are on it, but never to a rating below the number of cars already rolling, so no admitted car is stranded.

The subtle part is that a car's private view is a snapshot: between the read and the swap another car may have taken and even released the blaster, and the rating may have changed underneath both of them. Only the swap's re-check of the register keeps two cars from both believing they own the blaster.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A car is in the blast stage exactly when the compare-and-swap register names it, so the single-valued register admits at most one car under the blaster at any instant.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car eventually gets through the blaster and finishes the wash.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m4p0t0 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Vans, Tickets, QCap, NoVan, NoTicket

VARIABLES backlog, motor, vanState, carrying, closed
vars == <<backlog, motor, vanState, carrying, closed>>

\* Restock tickets sit in a bounded backlog; when it is full the dispatcher
\* simply cannot hand in another ticket, which is the backpressure.
\* The single hoist motor is the critical resource, and a van that dies while
\* holding it stays silent -- only the depot supervisor takes the motor back.
TypeOK ==
  /\ backlog \in Seq(Tickets)
  /\ Len(backlog) <= QCap
  /\ motor \in Vans \cup {NoVan}
  /\ vanState \in [Vans -> {"parked", "hoisting", "dead"}]
  /\ carrying \in [Vans -> Tickets \cup {NoTicket}]
  /\ closed \subseteq Tickets

Waiting == Tickets \ (closed \cup {carrying[v] : v \in Vans})

Init ==
  /\ backlog = << >>
  /\ motor = NoVan
  /\ vanState = [v \in Vans |-> "parked"]
  /\ carrying = [v \in Vans |-> NoTicket]
  /\ closed = {}

HandIn(t) ==
  /\ t \in Waiting
  /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(backlog) : backlog[i] # t
  /\ Len(backlog) < QCap
  /\ backlog' = Append(backlog, t)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<motor, vanState, carrying, closed>>

TakeHoist(v) ==
  /\ vanState[v] = "parked"
  /\ motor = NoVan
  /\ backlog # << >>
  /\ motor' = v
  /\ vanState' = [vanState EXCEPT ![v] = "hoisting"]
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![v] = Head(backlog)]
  /\ backlog' = Tail(backlog)
  /\ UNCHANGED closed

Restock(v) ==
  /\ vanState[v] = "hoisting"
  /\ motor = v
  /\ closed' = closed \cup {carrying[v]}
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![v] = NoTicket]
  /\ vanState' = [vanState EXCEPT ![v] = "parked"]
  /\ motor' = NoVan
  /\ UNCHANGED backlog

GoSilent(v) ==
  /\ vanState[v] = "hoisting"
  /\ vanState' = [vanState EXCEPT ![v] = "dead"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, motor, carrying, closed>>

TakeBack(v) ==
  /\ vanState[v] = "dead"
  /\ motor = v
  /\ Len(backlog) < QCap
  /\ backlog' = Append(backlog, carrying[v])
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![v] = NoTicket]
  /\ motor' = NoVan
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vanState, closed>>

Revive(v) ==
  /\ vanState[v] = "dead"
  /\ motor # v
  /\ carrying[v] = NoTicket
  /\ vanState' = [vanState EXCEPT ![v] = "parked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, motor, carrying, closed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Tickets : HandIn(t)
  \/ \E v \in Vans : TakeHoist(v) \/ Restock(v) \/ GoSilent(v)
                     \/ TakeBack(v) \/ Revive(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Exclusion: any van actually turning the hoist must be the van the motor
\* grant names, and the grant is single-valued, so two vans cannot both hoist.
HoistExclusive == \A v \in Vans : vanState[v] = "hoisting" => motor = v
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Vans = {v1, v2}
  Tickets = {t1, t2}
  NoVan = nobody
  NoTicket = nothing
  QCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT HoistExclusive
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked by service vans working out of one depot. Restock tickets are handed in to a backlog of bounded length; when the backlog is full the dispatcher simply cannot hand in another ticket, which is the backpressure that keeps the depot from over-committing. The depot has exactly one hoist motor, and it is the critical resource: only the van the motor grant names may actually be turning the hoist. A van can also die silently in the field while it is mid-restock, in which case it stops doing anything at all and never gives the grant back on its own.

The full action set is: HandIn -- the dispatcher appends a restock ticket that is neither already closed nor already in a van's hands nor already sitting in the backlog, but only while the backlog is below its cap. TakeHoist -- a parked van takes the motor grant when the grant is free and the backlog is non-empty, pulling the head ticket off the backlog and carrying it. Restock -- the van the motor grant names completes its ticket, closes it, parks again and gives the grant back. GoSilent -- a van that is mid-hoist dies without warning; it keeps the grant and keeps the ticket it was carrying, and takes no further action of its own. TakeBack -- the depot supervisor notices a dead van still named by the grant, frees the grant and pushes that van's ticket back onto the backlog, which it can only do if the backlog has room. Revive -- a dead van that no longer holds the grant and no longer carries a ticket is brought back and parks.

The hazard is that a silently dead van looks, from the outside, exactly like a van that is simply slow. If the grant could be handed to a second van before the supervisor had actually taken it back from the dead one, two vans could believe they were entitled to turn the same hoist.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any van that is actually turning the hoist is the van named by the single-valued motor grant, so no two vans can be hoisting at the same time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m9p4t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS FleetA, FleetB, Bays, MaxEpoch, QuotaHi

Robots == FleetA \cup FleetB

VARIABLES epoch, quotaA, quotaB, botState, grantEpoch
vars == <<epoch, quotaA, quotaB, botState, grantEpoch>>

\* Two fleet controllers plan independently but berth into one shared charging
\* pool. Each controller only ever sees its own quota, so the whole safety
\* argument rests on the epoch handshake: a berth grant carries the epoch it
\* was cut under and is worthless once the plan moves on.
BerthedA == Cardinality({r \in FleetA : botState[r] = "berthed"})
BerthedB == Cardinality({r \in FleetB : botState[r] = "berthed"})
ClaimA   == Cardinality({r \in FleetA : botState[r] \in {"granted", "berthed"}})
ClaimB   == Cardinality({r \in FleetB : botState[r] \in {"granted", "berthed"}})

Quota(r) == IF r \in FleetA THEN quotaA ELSE quotaB
Claim(r) == IF r \in FleetA THEN ClaimA ELSE ClaimB

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ quotaA \in 1 .. QuotaHi
  /\ quotaB \in 1 .. QuotaHi
  /\ botState \in [Robots -> {"roaming", "granted", "berthed", "charged"}]
  /\ grantEpoch \in [Robots -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ quotaA = 1
  /\ quotaB = 1
  /\ botState = [r \in Robots |-> "roaming"]
  /\ grantEpoch = [r \in Robots |-> 0]

CutGrant(r) ==
  /\ botState[r] = "roaming"
  /\ Claim(r) < Quota(r)
  /\ botState' = [botState EXCEPT ![r] = "granted"]
  /\ grantEpoch' = [grantEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quotaA, quotaB>>

Berth(r) ==
  /\ botState[r] = "granted"
  /\ grantEpoch[r] = epoch
  /\ botState' = [botState EXCEPT ![r] = "berthed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quotaA, quotaB, grantEpoch>>

VoidGrant(r) ==
  /\ botState[r] = "granted"
  /\ grantEpoch[r] # epoch
  /\ botState' = [botState EXCEPT ![r] = "roaming"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quotaA, quotaB, grantEpoch>>

Unberth(r) ==
  /\ botState[r] = "berthed"
  /\ botState' = [botState EXCEPT ![r] = "charged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quotaA, quotaB, grantEpoch>>

\* A reconfiguration bumps the epoch, which kills every outstanding grant, and
\* re-splits the shared pool -- never handing a controller a share smaller than
\* what its robots already occupy, and never splitting more than the pool holds.
Reconfigure(qa, qb) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ qa + qb <= Bays
  /\ qa >= BerthedA
  /\ qb >= BerthedB
  /\ <<qa, qb>> # <<quotaA, quotaB>>
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ quotaA' = qa
  /\ quotaB' = qb
  /\ UNCHANGED <<botState, grantEpoch>>

CutStep     == \E r \in Robots : CutGrant(r)
BerthStep   == \E r \in Robots : Berth(r)
VoidStep    == \E r \in Robots : VoidGrant(r)
UnberthStep == \E r \in Robots : Unberth(r)

Next == CutStep \/ BerthStep \/ VoidStep \/ UnberthStep
        \/ \E qa, qb \in 1 .. QuotaHi : Reconfigure(qa, qb)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(CutStep) /\ WF_vars(BerthStep)
        /\ WF_vars(VoidStep) /\ WF_vars(UnberthStep)

\* Capacity: the two independently planned fleets never together occupy more
\* charging bays than the shared pool physically has.
PoolNotOversubscribed == BerthedA + BerthedB <= Bays

EveryRobotCharged == <>(\A r \in Robots : botState[r] = "charged")
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  FleetA = {a1, a2}
  FleetB = {b1}
  Bays = 3
  MaxEpoch = 2
  QuotaHi = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PoolNotOversubscribed
PROPERTY EveryRobotCharged
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse runs two robot fleets under two independent fleet controllers, but both fleets berth into one shared pool of charging bays. Neither controller can see the other's robots; each is only told a quota, its share of the shared pool. The plan that fixes the two quotas carries an epoch number, and every berth grant a controller cuts is stamped with the epoch it was cut under. Bumping the epoch is what makes an outstanding grant worthless.

The full action set is: CutGrant -- a controller cuts a berth grant for one of its roaming robots, but only while that fleet's outstanding claims, meaning its granted plus already berthed robots, are strictly under its quota; the grant is stamped with the current epoch. Berth -- a robot with a grant whose stamp still matches the live epoch takes a bay and starts charging. VoidGrant -- a robot whose grant stamp no longer matches the live epoch throws the grant away and goes back to roaming, never having taken a bay. Unberth -- a berthed robot finishes charging, frees its bay and retires from the pool. Reconfigure -- the warehouse installs a new split of the pool: it bumps the epoch, which invalidates every outstanding grant at once, and it may only install a split whose two shares add up to no more than the physical pool, with neither share smaller than the robots that fleet already has standing in bays.

The hazard is exactly that the two controllers plan blind. If a reconfiguration were allowed to hand one controller a larger share while the other fleet still had robots physically standing in bays that the new split no longer accounts for, both controllers could fill up to their own quotas and the shared pool would be oversubscribed even though neither controller ever exceeded the number it was given.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of robots standing in charging bays, counting both independently planned fleets together, never exceeds the number of bays the shared pool physically has.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every robot eventually finishes charging and retires from the pool.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m2p3t2 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS CoordA, CoordB, Slots, Racks, NoDeal, NoSlot

Deals == CoordA \cup CoordB

VARIABLES phase, target, penciled, holder
vars == <<phase, target, penciled, holder>>

\* Two restock coordinators drive deals against one shared slot pool. Each deal
\* runs two-phase commit: it pencils its slot in on every rack, and may only
\* commit once every rack has that deal, and no other, penciled in.
Unanimous(d) == \A k \in Racks : penciled[k][target[d]] = d

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Deals -> {"fresh", "voting", "sealed", "spent", "torn"}]
  /\ target \in [Deals -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ penciled \in [Racks -> [Slots -> Deals \cup {NoDeal}]]
  /\ holder \in [Slots -> Deals \cup {NoDeal}]

Init ==
  /\ phase = [d \in Deals |-> "fresh"]
  /\ target = [d \in Deals |-> NoSlot]
  /\ penciled = [k \in Racks |-> [s \in Slots |-> NoDeal]]
  /\ holder = [s \in Slots |-> NoDeal]

Open(d, s) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "fresh"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "voting"]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![d] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<penciled, holder>>

Pencil(d, k) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "voting"
  /\ penciled[k][target[d]] = NoDeal
  /\ holder[target[d]] = NoDeal
  /\ penciled' = [penciled EXCEPT ![k][target[d]] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, target, holder>>

Seal(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "voting"
  /\ Unanimous(d)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "sealed"]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![target[d]] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, penciled>>

Erase(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] \in {"voting", "sealed"}
  /\ penciled' = [k \in Racks |-> [s \in Slots |->
                     IF penciled[k][s] = d THEN NoDeal ELSE penciled[k][s]]]
  /\ penciled' # penciled
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, target, holder>>

Tear(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "voting"
  /\ \E k \in Racks : penciled[k][target[d]] \notin {NoDeal, d}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "torn"]
  /\ penciled' = [k \in Racks |-> [s \in Slots |->
                     IF penciled[k][s] = d THEN NoDeal ELSE penciled[k][s]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, holder>>

Vend(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "sealed"
  /\ holder[target[d]] = d
  /\ \A k \in Racks : penciled[k][target[d]] # d
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "spent"]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![target[d]] = NoDeal]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, penciled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Deals, s \in Slots : Open(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Deals, k \in Racks : Pencil(d, k)
  \/ \E d \in Deals : Seal(d) \/ Erase(d) \/ Tear(d) \/ Vend(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a sealed deal really is the recorded holder of the
\* slot it targeted, so two sealed deals can never be sitting on one slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A d \in Deals : phase[d] = "sealed" => holder[target[d]] = d
=======================================================================
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked by two independent regional coordinators. They do not talk to each other, yet they draw from one shared pool of machine slots, and every allocation has to be agreed by every rack controller in the network. Each coordinator therefore runs its restock deals as a two-phase commit: first it pencils its chosen slot in on each rack, and only when every rack carries that pencil mark, and nobody else's, may it seal the deal and become the recorded holder of the slot.

The full action set is: Open -- a coordinator opens a fresh deal and names the slot it is going after, moving the deal into voting. Pencil -- a voting deal gets penciled in on one rack for its target slot, which is possible only if that rack has no other pencil mark on that slot and the slot has no recorded holder. Seal -- a voting deal that is penciled in on every rack, unanimously, commits: it becomes the recorded holder of its target slot. Erase -- the pencil marks belonging to a deal are rubbed out across all racks, which is the second-phase cleanup after sealing and also the way a voting deal can back off. Tear -- a voting deal that finds some rack already penciled for a different deal tears itself up, rubbing out its own marks. Vend -- a sealed deal whose pencil marks have all been rubbed out is dispensed, releasing the slot back to the pool with no recorded holder.

The hazard is double allocation. Because the two coordinators are independent, they can both be chasing the same slot at the same moment; only unanimity across the racks decides which one is entitled to it. A deal that sealed on partial agreement would leave two coordinators each convinced it owned the slot, and the slot's record could only name one of them.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every sealed deal is the slot record's own named holder for the slot it targeted, so no slot can ever be carrying two sealed deals at once.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m4p6t1 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Machines, QCap, MaxSeq, MaxGen

Orders == [mach : Machines, gen : 0 .. MaxGen, seq : 1 .. MaxSeq]

VARIABLES inflight, cred, stream, nextSeq
vars == <<inflight, cred, stream, nextSeq>>

\* Orders sit in an unordered bounded pouch, so they can be picked up in any
\* order; the pouch cap is the backpressure on the dispatcher.
\* Each order carries the credential generation it was cut under, and a machine
\* re-keys by bumping its credential, which retires everything already in the air.
TypeOK ==
  /\ inflight \subseteq Orders
  /\ Cardinality(inflight) <= QCap
  /\ cred \in [Machines -> 0 .. MaxGen]
  /\ stream \in [Machines -> Seq(Orders)]
  /\ nextSeq \in [Machines -> 1 .. (MaxSeq + 1)]

Init ==
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ cred = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ stream = [m \in Machines |-> << >>]
  /\ nextSeq = [m \in Machines |-> 1]

Cut(m) ==
  /\ Cardinality(inflight) < QCap
  /\ nextSeq[m] <= MaxSeq
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup
       {[mach |-> m, gen |-> cred[m], seq |-> nextSeq[m]]}
  /\ nextSeq' = [nextSeq EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, stream>>

Rekey(m) ==
  /\ cred[m] < MaxGen
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
  /\ stream' = [stream EXCEPT ![m] = << >>]
  /\ nextSeq' = [nextSeq EXCEPT ![m] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED inflight

Obey(o) ==
  /\ o \in inflight
  /\ o.gen = cred[o.mach]
  /\ o.seq = Len(stream[o.mach]) + 1
  /\ stream' = [stream EXCEPT ![o.mach] = Append(@, o)]
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, nextSeq>>

Refuse(o) ==
  /\ o \in inflight
  /\ o.gen # cred[o.mach]
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, stream, nextSeq>>

CutStep    == \E m \in Machines : Cut(m)
RekeyStep  == \E m \in Machines : Rekey(m)
ObeyStep   == \E o \in Orders : Obey(o)
RefuseStep == \E o \in Orders : Refuse(o)

Next == CutStep \/ RekeyStep \/ ObeyStep \/ RefuseStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ObeyStep) /\ WF_vars(RefuseStep)

\* Nothing a machine has acted on came from a retired credential, and nothing
\* landed out of position: each machine's obeyed stream is a gap-free run of
\* orders all bearing the credential the machine is holding right now.
StreamIntegrity ==
  \A m \in Machines :
    \A i \in 1 .. Len(stream[m]) :
      /\ stream[m][i].seq = i
      /\ stream[m][i].gen = cred[m]
      /\ stream[m][i].mach = m

PouchDrains == (inflight # {}) ~> (inflight = {})
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Machines = {m1, m2}
  QCap = 2
  MaxSeq = 2
  MaxGen = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StreamIntegrity
PROPERTY PouchDrains
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network is driven by a central dispatcher that cuts restock orders into a shared pouch of orders still in the air. The pouch holds only so many orders at once, and the dispatcher cannot cut another one while it is full -- that cap is the backpressure. The pouch is unordered: an order that was cut first is not necessarily the one a machine picks up first, so orders arrive at the machines in any order at all. Every order carries two things: the position it occupies in that machine's order stream, and the credential generation the dispatcher was holding for that machine when the order was cut. A machine that re-keys bumps its credential generation, which retires in one stroke every order for it that is still in the air, and starts its stream over from the first position.

The full action set is: Cut -- the dispatcher cuts the next order for a machine into the pouch, stamped with that machine's current credential generation and with the next unused position, allowed only while the pouch is below its cap and the machine's stream has not run out of positions. Rekey -- a machine bumps its own credential generation, clears its obeyed stream and tells the dispatcher to start numbering that machine's positions from the beginning again. Obey -- a machine picks any order out of the pouch addressed to it, and acts on it only if the order bears exactly the credential generation the machine is holding right now and sits in exactly the next open position of that machine's stream; the order is then appended to the stream and leaves the pouch. Refuse -- a machine picks an order out of the pouch whose credential generation no longer matches its own, and throws it away without acting on it.

The hazard is an order cut by a dispatcher that was working from a credential the machine has since retired: because the pouch is unordered, such an order can sit around and surface long after the re-key, looking perfectly well-formed. Acting on it would be a machine taking instruction from a stale authority, and it would also punch a hole in the machine's position numbering.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every machine, each order in the stream it has acted on sits in its own correct position with no gaps, is addressed to that machine, and bears exactly the credential generation the machine currently holds, so no retired or misaddressed order has ever been obeyed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the pouch holds orders, every one of them is eventually either obeyed or refused, so the pouch always empties again.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m8p2t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Sections, Marks, Clerks, Stock, NoOne

Titles == Sections \X Marks

VARIABLES secLatch, titleLatch, onShelf, onHold, lentOut
vars == <<secLatch, titleLatch, onShelf, onHold, lentOut>>

\* Every physical copy of a title is in exactly one of three places, and each
\* staff move is a hand-off of one copy from one place to another -- copies are
\* never conjured up and never lost, only relocated.
\* Clerks must latch a whole section before latching a title inside it, and the
\* head librarian's override moves copies without latching anything.
Placed(t) == onShelf[t] + onHold[t] + lentOut[t]

TypeOK ==
  /\ secLatch \in [Sections -> Clerks \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ titleLatch \in [Titles -> Clerks \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ onShelf \in [Titles -> 0 .. Stock]
  /\ onHold \in [Titles -> 0 .. Stock]
  /\ lentOut \in [Titles -> 0 .. Stock]

Init ==
  /\ secLatch = [s \in Sections |-> NoOne]
  /\ titleLatch = [t \in Titles |-> NoOne]
  /\ onShelf = [t \in Titles |-> Stock]
  /\ onHold = [t \in Titles |-> 0]
  /\ lentOut = [t \in Titles |-> 0]

Owns(c, t) == secLatch[t[1]] = c /\ titleLatch[t] = c

LatchSection(c, s) ==
  /\ secLatch[s] = NoOne
  /\ \A x \in Sections : secLatch[x] # c
  /\ secLatch' = [secLatch EXCEPT ![s] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<titleLatch, onShelf, onHold, lentOut>>

LatchTitle(c, t) ==
  /\ secLatch[t[1]] = c
  /\ titleLatch[t] = NoOne
  /\ titleLatch' = [titleLatch EXCEPT ![t] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<secLatch, onShelf, onHold, lentOut>>

Reserve(c, t) ==
  /\ Owns(c, t)
  /\ onShelf[t] > 0
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
  /\ onHold' = [onHold EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<secLatch, titleLatch, lentOut>>

Lend(c, t) ==
  /\ Owns(c, t)
  /\ onHold[t] > 0
  /\ onHold' = [onHold EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
  /\ lentOut' = [lentOut EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<secLatch, titleLatch, onShelf>>

BookDrop(t) ==
  /\ lentOut[t] > 0
  /\ lentOut' = [lentOut EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<secLatch, titleLatch, onHold>>

UnlatchTitle(c, t) ==
  /\ titleLatch[t] = c
  /\ titleLatch' = [titleLatch EXCEPT ![t] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<secLatch, onShelf, onHold, lentOut>>

UnlatchSection(c, s) ==
  /\ secLatch[s] = c
  /\ \A m \in Marks : titleLatch[<<s, m>>] = NoOne
  /\ secLatch' = [secLatch EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<titleLatch, onShelf, onHold, lentOut>>

Override(t) ==
  /\ onHold[t] > 0
  /\ onHold' = [onHold EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<secLatch, titleLatch, lentOut>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Clerks, s \in Sections : LatchSection(c, s) \/ UnlatchSection(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Clerks, t \in Titles :
        LatchTitle(c, t) \/ Reserve(c, t) \/ Lend(c, t) \/ UnlatchTitle(c, t)
  \/ \E t \in Titles : BookDrop(t) \/ Override(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: the copies of each title are only ever relocated between the
\* open shelf, the hold shelf and borrowers -- never created, never destroyed.
CopiesConserved == \A t \in Titles : Placed(t) = Stock
=======================================================================
nl:
A library reservation system tracks the physical copies of every title it stocks. A title lives at a shelf mark inside a section, and each of its copies is, at any moment, in exactly one of three places: standing on the open shelf, waiting on the hold shelf for a reader who reserved it, or out with a borrower. Every move a clerk makes is a hand-off of one single copy from one of those places to another, which is the only way the counts are ever allowed to change. Clerks work under a two-level discipline: a clerk latches a whole section before latching any individual title inside that section, holds at most one section at a time, and gives every title back before giving the section back. The head librarian has an override that moves copies without latching anything at all.

The full action set is: LatchSection -- a clerk latches a free section, provided it holds no other section. LatchTitle -- a clerk holding a section latches a free title inside that section. Reserve -- a clerk holding both the section and the title takes one copy off the open shelf and stands it on the hold shelf. Lend -- a clerk holding both latches takes one copy off the hold shelf and gives it to a borrower. BookDrop -- a borrower returns a copy through the drop box, which puts it straight back on the open shelf and needs no latch at all. UnlatchTitle -- a clerk gives a title latch back. UnlatchSection -- a clerk gives the section latch back, which it may only do once every title in that section is unlatched. Override -- the head librarian pulls a copy off the hold shelf back onto the open shelf, ignoring every latch that may be held.

What matters here is not who is holding which latch; it is that each of these moves is a genuine relocation. The book drop and the head librarian's override both act outside the latching discipline, and either of them could quietly break the books if it added a copy in one place without taking it away from another.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every title, the number of copies on the open shelf plus those on the hold shelf plus those out with borrowers always equals the number of copies the library stocks of that title, so no copy is ever created or destroyed by any move.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m4p0t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cars, Boss, Free, QCap, OverrideBudget

Users == Cars \cup {Boss}

VARIABLES lane, pit, phase, overrides
vars == <<lane, pit, phase, overrides>>

\* The undercarriage rinse pit takes one user at a time. Cars reach it only
\* through a bounded holding lane -- when the lane is full nothing more may be
\* let in, which is the backpressure. The shift manager bypasses the lane
\* entirely, but only against a fixed override budget.
TypeOK ==
  /\ lane \in Seq(Cars)
  /\ Len(lane) <= QCap
  /\ pit \in Users \cup {Free}
  /\ phase \in [Users -> {"outside", "laned", "rinsing", "washed", "resting"}]
  /\ overrides \in 0 .. OverrideBudget

Init ==
  /\ lane = << >>
  /\ pit = Free
  /\ phase = [u \in Users |-> IF u = Boss THEN "resting" ELSE "outside"]
  /\ overrides = 0

JoinLane(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "outside"
  /\ Len(lane) < QCap
  /\ lane' = Append(lane, c)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "laned"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pit, overrides>>

RollIn(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "laned"
  /\ lane # << >>
  /\ Head(lane) = c
  /\ pit = Free
  /\ pit' = c
  /\ lane' = Tail(lane)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "rinsing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED overrides

RollOut(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "rinsing"
  /\ pit = c
  /\ pit' = Free
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "washed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lane, overrides>>

\* Override one: the manager drops straight into a free pit for a service run.
Seize ==
  /\ phase[Boss] = "resting"
  /\ pit = Free
  /\ overrides < OverrideBudget
  /\ pit' = Boss
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![Boss] = "rinsing"]
  /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED lane

StandDown ==
  /\ phase[Boss] = "rinsing"
  /\ pit = Boss
  /\ pit' = Free
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![Boss] = "resting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lane, overrides>>

\* Override two: the manager evicts whoever is mid-rinse, sending that car back
\* outside to line up again. Also charged against the same budget.
Evict(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "rinsing"
  /\ pit = c
  /\ overrides < OverrideBudget
  /\ pit' = Free
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "outside"]
  /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED lane

JoinStep  == \E c \in Cars : JoinLane(c)
InStep    == \E c \in Cars : RollIn(c)
OutStep   == \E c \in Cars : RollOut(c)
EvictStep == \E c \in Cars : Evict(c)

Next == JoinStep \/ InStep \/ OutStep \/ EvictStep \/ Seize \/ StandDown

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(JoinStep) /\ WF_vars(InStep) /\ WF_vars(OutStep)
        /\ WF_vars(StandDown)

\* Exclusion: anyone actually being rinsed is the single user the pit names,
\* manager included, so two users can never share the pit.
PitExclusive == \A u \in Users : phase[u] = "rinsing" => pit = u

EveryCarWashed == <>(\A c \in Cars : phase[c] = "washed")
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {c1, c2}
  Boss = shiftmgr
  Free = empty
  QCap = 2
  OverrideBudget = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PitExclusive
PROPERTY EveryCarWashed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line ends at a single undercarriage rinse pit. The pit is the critical resource: exactly one user may be down in it at a time. Cars reach the pit only through a holding lane of bounded length, first in and first out; when the lane is full no further car may be let in, and that is the backpressure the line uses to stop itself from over-committing. The shift manager is privileged: he does not queue at all, and he can also pull a car out mid-rinse. Both of his privileged moves are charged against a fixed override budget for the shift, so he cannot keep doing them forever.

The full action set is: JoinLane -- a car outside the wash joins the tail of the holding lane, but only while the lane is under its length cap. RollIn -- the car at the head of the lane rolls down into the pit when the pit is free, and leaves the lane. RollOut -- the car in the pit finishes its rinse, comes up and leaves the pit free. Seize -- the shift manager drops straight into a free pit for a service run, bypassing the lane completely, and spends one unit of the override budget. StandDown -- the manager finishes his service run and comes back up, leaving the pit free. Evict -- the manager pulls whichever car is mid-rinse out of the pit and sends it back outside to line up again from scratch, also spending one unit of the override budget.

The point of interest is that the manager reaches the pit by a completely different path from the cars: he never touches the lane, and the lane's discipline therefore says nothing about him. The pit's own occupancy record is the only thing standing between a service run and a car both being down in the pit at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Anyone actually being rinsed, car or shift manager, is exactly the single user the pit's occupancy record names, so two users can never be down in the pit at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car eventually completes its rinse and comes up washed.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m5p3t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, Windows, Relays, NoWindow, NoFeeder, NoTask

Errand == (Feeders \X Windows) \cup {NoTask}

VARIABLES asked, errand, ballots, holds
vars == <<asked, errand, ballots, holds>>

\* Every shed window is handed out by majority vote of the relay controllers.
\* A relay is slow, never dead: it copies a feeder's request onto its clipboard
\* and may only get around to casting that ballot after the request has moved on.
Backers(w, f) == Cardinality({k \in Relays : ballots[w][k] = f})
Majority(w, f) == 2 * Backers(w, f) > Cardinality(Relays)

TypeOK ==
  /\ asked \in [Feeders -> Windows \cup {NoWindow}]
  /\ errand \in [Relays -> Errand]
  /\ ballots \in [Windows -> [Relays -> Feeders \cup {NoFeeder}]]
  /\ holds \in [Feeders -> Windows \cup {NoWindow}]

Init ==
  /\ asked = [f \in Feeders |-> NoWindow]
  /\ errand = [k \in Relays |-> NoTask]
  /\ ballots = [w \in Windows |-> [k \in Relays |-> NoFeeder]]
  /\ holds = [f \in Feeders |-> NoWindow]

Ask(f, w) ==
  /\ holds[f] = NoWindow
  /\ asked[f] # w
  /\ asked' = [asked EXCEPT ![f] = w]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<errand, ballots, holds>>

Copy(k, f) ==
  /\ errand[k] = NoTask
  /\ asked[f] # NoWindow
  /\ errand' = [errand EXCEPT ![k] = <<f, asked[f]>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<asked, ballots, holds>>

Cast(k) ==
  /\ errand[k] # NoTask
  /\ ballots[errand[k][2]][k] = NoFeeder
  /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![errand[k][2]][k] = errand[k][1]]
  /\ errand' = [errand EXCEPT ![k] = NoTask]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<asked, holds>>

Tear(k) ==
  /\ errand[k] # NoTask
  /\ ballots[errand[k][2]][k] # NoFeeder
  /\ errand' = [errand EXCEPT ![k] = NoTask]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<asked, ballots, holds>>

Award(f, w) ==
  /\ holds[f] = NoWindow
  /\ asked[f] = w
  /\ Majority(w, f)
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = w]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<asked, errand, ballots>>

Shed(f) ==
  /\ holds[f] # NoWindow
  /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![holds[f]] = [k \in Relays |-> NoFeeder]]
  /\ asked' = [asked EXCEPT ![f] = NoWindow]
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = NoWindow]
  /\ UNCHANGED errand

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, w \in Windows : Ask(f, w) \/ Award(f, w)
  \/ \E k \in Relays, f \in Feeders : Copy(k, f)
  \/ \E k \in Relays : Cast(k) \/ Tear(k)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : Shed(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a feeder only ever holds a shed window that a strict
\* majority of relays is currently backing it for. Since a relay casts one
\* ballot per window, two feeders can never both be majority-backed there.
WindowQuorumBacked ==
  \A f \in Feeders : holds[f] # NoWindow => Majority(holds[f], f)
========================================================================
nl:
A power-grid load shedder decides which feeder gets to drop load in which shed window. No single operator can make that call: a feeder is awarded a window only when a strict majority of the relay controllers is backing it for that window. Each relay controller casts at most one ballot per window. The controllers are slow but never failed -- a controller copies a feeder's request onto its clipboard and then gets around to casting the ballot some time later, by which point the feeder may well have asked for a different window instead.

The full action set is: Ask -- a feeder that currently holds no window changes the window it is asking for. Copy -- a relay controller with an empty clipboard copies down one feeder's current request, feeder and window together. Cast -- a relay controller casts the ballot on its clipboard, marking that window with that feeder, provided it has not already balloted in that window; the clipboard is then empty again. Note that the request it copied may have moved on in the meantime, so the ballot can be for a window the feeder no longer wants. Tear -- a relay controller tears up a clipboard entry for a window it has already balloted in, without casting anything. Award -- a feeder holding no window is awarded the window it is currently asking for, but only if a strict majority of the relay controllers is backing it for that window right now. Shed -- a feeder that holds a window drops its load, gives the window back, and the ballots for that window are wiped so the window can be contested again.

The hazard is double allocation of one shed window. Two feeders contesting the same window will both accumulate ballots, and the slow controllers make it easy for the tallies to look tempting before they are decisive. Only the fact that no controller can back two different feeders in one window, and that awarding requires a strict majority, keeps two feeders from being handed the same window and shedding into each other.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any feeder holding a shed window is backed for that window by a strict majority of the relay controllers, and since each controller ballots for at most one feeder per window, no window can ever be held by two feeders at once.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m1p2t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS RingSize, SplitAt, Stock, Batch, Home

Nodes == 1 .. RingSize
Downstream(n) == (n % RingSize) + 1
Instance(n) == IF n <= SplitAt THEN "front" ELSE "back"

VARIABLES baton, hopper, reserve, press, bin
vars == <<baton, hopper, reserve, press, bin>>

\* Two spooler instances, a front-office one and a back-office one, own
\* different stretches of one ring of spool nodes but draw paper from a single
\* shared hopper. Sheets are only ever moved from one holding place to another:
\* hopper, a node's own reserve, the press, and the output bin.
Onhand == hopper + press + bin +
          (LET RECURSIVE Pile(_)
               Pile(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
                          ELSE LET n == CHOOSE m \in S : TRUE
                               IN reserve[n] + Pile(S \ {n})
           IN Pile(Nodes))

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Nodes
  /\ hopper \in 0 .. Stock
  /\ reserve \in [Nodes -> 0 .. Stock]
  /\ press \in 0 .. Stock
  /\ bin \in 0 .. Stock

Init ==
  /\ baton = Home
  /\ hopper = Stock
  /\ reserve = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
  /\ press = 0
  /\ bin = 0

PassBaton ==
  /\ baton' = Downstream(baton)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, reserve, press, bin>>

Draw(n, k) ==
  /\ baton = n
  /\ hopper >= k
  /\ reserve[n] + k <= Stock
  /\ hopper' = hopper - k
  /\ reserve' = [reserve EXCEPT ![n] = @ + k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, press, bin>>

Feed(n, k) ==
  /\ baton = n
  /\ reserve[n] >= k
  /\ press + k <= Stock
  /\ reserve' = [reserve EXCEPT ![n] = @ - k]
  /\ press' = press + k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, hopper, bin>>

Impress(k) ==
  /\ press >= k
  /\ bin + k <= Stock
  /\ press' = press - k
  /\ bin' = bin + k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, hopper, reserve>>

Pulp(k) ==
  /\ bin >= k
  /\ hopper + k <= Stock
  /\ bin' = bin - k
  /\ hopper' = hopper + k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, reserve, press>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E n \in Nodes, k \in 1 .. Batch : Draw(n, k) \/ Feed(n, k)
  \/ \E k \in 1 .. Batch : Impress(k) \/ Pulp(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(PassBaton)

\* Conservation: the shop's sheet count never changes. Every action is a
\* hand-off of sheets between holding places, never a creation or a loss.
SheetsConserved == Onhand = Stock

BatonComesHome == (baton # Home) ~> (baton = Home)
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  RingSize = 3
  SplitAt = 1
  Stock = 3
  Batch = 2
  Home = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SheetsConserved
PROPERTY BatonComesHome
nl:
A print shop runs two spooler instances, a front-office one and a back-office one. They are independent programs and neither knows what the other is doing, but their spool nodes sit on one shared ring and they draw paper from one shared hopper. A baton travels around the ring, and only the node currently holding the baton may move paper into or out of its own reserve. Sheets in the shop live in exactly four kinds of place: the shared hopper, the private reserve of each spool node, the press, and the output bin.

The full action set is: PassBaton -- the baton moves from its current node to the next node downstream on the ring, wrapping around at the end. Draw -- the node holding the baton takes a batch of sheets out of the shared hopper and into its own reserve, which it can only do if the hopper actually has that many. Feed -- the node holding the baton pushes a batch of sheets out of its own reserve into the press. Impress -- the press prints a batch of sheets and moves them into the output bin. Pulp -- a batch of sheets is taken out of the output bin and put back into the shared hopper for reuse.

What matters about this shop is not who holds the baton. It is that the shop owns a fixed quantity of paper, and every single one of these moves is a hand-off: sheets leave one place exactly as many as arrive in another. Because two independent instances are drawing from one hopper, a move that took sheets out of the hopper without adding them to a reserve, or that added to the press without taking from a reserve, would quietly change the shop's paper count with nobody in a position to notice.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of sheets in the shared hopper, plus those in every spool node's reserve, plus those in the press, plus those in the output bin always equals the fixed quantity of paper the shop owns, so no sheet is ever created or destroyed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The baton always eventually comes back around the ring to the home node.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m5p3t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Slots, Agents, NoBank, WireCap, MaxRound

Notes == [agent : Agents, slot : Slots, bank : Banks, rnd : 0 .. MaxRound]

VARIABLES wire, tally, booked, round
vars == <<wire, tally, booked, round>>

\* Settlement agents post their votes as notes onto an unordered wire, so notes
\* land in any order and a note can surface long after its round has closed.
\* A slot is bookable only for a bank a strict majority of agents has voted for.
Backers(s, b) == Cardinality({a \in Agents : tally[s][a] = b})
Certified == {p \in Slots \X Banks : 2 * Backers(p[1], p[2]) > Cardinality(Agents)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ wire \subseteq Notes
  /\ Cardinality(wire) <= WireCap
  /\ tally \in [Slots -> [Agents -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]]
  /\ booked \subseteq Slots \X Banks
  /\ round \in [Slots -> 0 .. MaxRound]

Init ==
  /\ wire = {}
  /\ tally = [s \in Slots |-> [a \in Agents |-> NoBank]]
  /\ booked = {}
  /\ round = [s \in Slots |-> 0]

Post(a, s, b) ==
  /\ Cardinality(wire) < WireCap
  /\ wire' = wire \cup
       {[agent |-> a, slot |-> s, bank |-> b, rnd |-> round[s]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, booked, round>>

Record(n) ==
  /\ n \in wire
  /\ n.rnd = round[n.slot]
  /\ tally[n.slot][n.agent] = NoBank
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![n.slot][n.agent] = n.bank]
  /\ wire' = wire \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, round>>

Bin(n) ==
  /\ n \in wire
  /\ \/ n.rnd # round[n.slot]
     \/ tally[n.slot][n.agent] # NoBank
  /\ wire' = wire \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, booked, round>>

Book(s, b) ==
  /\ <<s, b>> \notin booked
  /\ <<s, b>> \in Certified
  /\ booked' = booked \cup {<<s, b>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wire, tally, round>>

Settle(s, b) ==
  /\ <<s, b>> \in booked
  /\ round[s] < MaxRound
  /\ booked' = booked \ {<<s, b>>}
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = [a \in Agents |-> NoBank]]
  /\ round' = [round EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED wire

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Agents, s \in Slots, b \in Banks : Post(a, s, b)
  \/ \E n \in Notes : Record(n) \/ Bin(n)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Banks : Book(s, b) \/ Settle(s, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: every standing booking is one a strict majority of
\* agents is backing right now. An agent's vote in a slot is single-valued, so
\* two banks cannot both be certified for the same slot.
BookingsCertified == booked \subseteq Certified
========================================================================
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is divided into netting slots, and each slot has to be booked to exactly one member bank. No member decides this alone: settlement agents vote, and a slot is only bookable to a bank that a strict majority of the agents is backing for that slot. The agents do not talk to the batch controller directly. They post their votes as notes onto a wire, and the wire is unordered -- notes land in whatever order they happen to land in, so a note posted early can surface long after later notes have already been taken in. Each round of a slot closes when the slot settles, and notes carry the round they were posted under.

The full action set is: Post -- a settlement agent puts a note on the wire naming a slot and a bank, stamped with the round that slot is currently in, allowed only while the wire is under its capacity. Record -- the batch controller takes any note off the wire and enters it in the tally, but only if the note's round is still the slot's live round and that agent has not already been tallied in that slot; an agent's vote in a slot is therefore single-valued and first-entered wins. Bin -- the controller takes a note off the wire and throws it away, because its round has closed or that agent is already tallied in that slot. Book -- a slot is booked to a bank that a strict majority of the agents is currently backing for it. Settle -- a standing booking is settled: the booking is struck, the slot's tally is wiped clean, and the slot moves into its next round.

The hazard is double allocation of one netting slot. Because notes arrive in arbitrary order and can be stale by a whole round, the tally for a slot can look very different depending on which notes got taken in first. The only thing keeping two banks from both being booked into the same slot is that no agent's vote counts twice in a slot and that a booking needs a strict majority.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every booking standing in the batch is one whose bank is backed for that slot by a strict majority of the settlement agents at that moment, which rules out two banks holding the same netting slot.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m0p3t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Runners, Slots, MaxVer, Nobody, NoPeek

Peeks == (Slots \X (0 .. MaxVer)) \cup {NoPeek}

VARIABLES ver, owner, mode, peek
vars == <<ver, owner, mode, peek>>

\* Optimistic allocation: a runner peeks at a free slot together with the slot's
\* version stamp, then claims it only if the stamp has not moved. Every change
\* to who owns a slot moves the stamp, which is what makes a stale peek visible.
\* A runner can also go dark at any moment without telling anyone.
TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in [Slots -> 0 .. MaxVer]
  /\ owner \in [Slots -> Runners \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ mode \in [Runners -> {"free", "peeked", "holding", "restocked", "dark"}]
  /\ peek \in [Runners -> Peeks]

Init ==
  /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Nobody]
  /\ mode = [r \in Runners |-> "free"]
  /\ peek = [r \in Runners |-> NoPeek]

Peek(r, s) ==
  /\ mode[r] = "free"
  /\ owner[s] = Nobody
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![r] = <<s, ver[s]>>]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "peeked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner>>

Claim(r) ==
  /\ mode[r] = "peeked"
  /\ ver[peek[r][1]] = peek[r][2]
  /\ ver[peek[r][1]] < MaxVer
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![peek[r][1]] = r]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![peek[r][1]] = @ + 1]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED peek

Retry(r) ==
  /\ mode[r] = "peeked"
  /\ ver[peek[r][1]] # peek[r][2]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "free"]
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![r] = NoPeek]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner>>

Restock(r) ==
  /\ mode[r] = "holding"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "restocked"]
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![r] = NoPeek]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner>>

GoDark(r) ==
  /\ mode[r] \in {"free", "peeked", "holding"}
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "dark"]
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![r] = NoPeek]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner>>

Sweep(s) ==
  /\ owner[s] # Nobody
  /\ mode[owner[s]] = "dark"
  /\ ver[s] < MaxVer
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, peek>>

PeekStep    == \E r \in Runners, s \in Slots : Peek(r, s)
ClaimStep   == \E r \in Runners : Claim(r)
RetryStep   == \E r \in Runners : Retry(r)
RestockStep == \E r \in Runners : Restock(r)

Next == PeekStep \/ ClaimStep \/ RetryStep \/ RestockStep
        \/ (\E r \in Runners : GoDark(r)) \/ (\E s \in Slots : Sweep(s))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(PeekStep) /\ WF_vars(ClaimStep)
        /\ WF_vars(RetryStep) /\ WF_vars(RestockStep)

\* No double allocation: a peek whose version stamp is still current is proof
\* that the slot is still unclaimed, so a claim made on a live peek can never
\* land on a slot somebody else already took.
PeekStillTrue ==
  \A r \in Runners :
    (mode[r] = "peeked" /\ ver[peek[r][1]] = peek[r][2])
      => owner[peek[r][1]] = Nobody

EveryRunnerSettles ==
  <>(\A r \in Runners : mode[r] \in {"restocked", "dark"})
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Runners = {r1, r2}
  Slots = {s1, s2}
  MaxVer = 3
  Nobody = unowned
  NoPeek = nothing

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PeekStillTrue
PROPERTY EveryRunnerSettles
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network hands out restock slots to field runners. There is no lock on a slot; instead the network works optimistically. A runner peeks at a slot that currently has no owner and writes down, along with the slot, the version stamp the slot carried at the moment of the peek. Later it tries to claim the slot, and the claim is only accepted if the slot's version stamp has not moved since the peek. Every single change to who owns a slot moves that slot's stamp, which is exactly what makes a stale peek detectable. Runners are unreliable: one can go dark at any moment, without warning and without telling anybody, and if it was holding a slot the slot stays nominally owned until the depot sweeps it.

The full action set is: Peek -- a free runner picks a slot that currently has no owner and writes down the slot together with its current version stamp. Claim -- a runner that has peeked takes ownership of the slot it peeked at, but only if the slot's stamp is still exactly the one it wrote down; the claim bumps the stamp. Retry -- a runner that has peeked notices the slot's stamp has moved, throws the peek away and starts over as a free runner. Restock -- a runner holding a slot finishes restocking it and is done, keeping the slot recorded to it. GoDark -- a runner in any working state dies silently and stops acting for good, dropping whatever peek it was carrying. Sweep -- the depot notices a slot recorded to a runner that has gone dark, clears the owner and bumps the stamp so the slot can be handed out again.

The hazard is double allocation of a slot. Two runners can peek the very same free slot at the very same stamp, and a runner that goes dark can leave the network unsure whether a slot is really in use. What makes it safe is that a peek is only ever good while the stamp it recorded is still the live one: the instant anybody takes or releases the slot, the stamp moves and every outstanding peek on that slot is worthless.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a runner is holding a peek whose recorded version stamp still matches the slot's live stamp, that slot genuinely has no owner, so a claim made on an unmoved stamp can never land on a slot somebody else has already taken.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every runner eventually settles, either finishing its restock or having gone dark.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p1t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Bots, Edits, TTL, NoBot, NoEdit

NoDraft == [ed |-> NoEdit, base |-> {}]
Drafts  == {NoDraft} \cup [ed : Edits, base : SUBSET Edits]

VARIABLES sheet, draft, acked, lease, alive
vars == <<sheet, draft, acked, lease, alive>>

\* The fleet keeps one shared count sheet for the aisle. A bot may only write
\* it while holding a live lease; the lease dies purely by running out of time,
\* which is also what covers a bot that has quietly stopped responding.
\* A write is a whole-sheet overwrite of what the bot read plus its own edit.
Live == lease.holder # NoBot /\ lease.ttl > 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ sheet \subseteq Edits
  /\ draft \in [Bots -> Drafts]
  /\ acked \subseteq Edits
  /\ lease \in [holder : Bots \cup {NoBot}, ttl : 0 .. TTL]
  /\ alive \subseteq Bots

Init ==
  /\ sheet = {}
  /\ draft = [b \in Bots |-> NoDraft]
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ lease = [holder |-> NoBot, ttl |-> 0]
  /\ alive = Bots

Take(b) ==
  /\ b \in alive
  /\ ~Live
  /\ draft[b] = NoDraft
  /\ lease' = [holder |-> b, ttl |-> TTL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, draft, acked, alive>>

Read(b, e) ==
  /\ b \in alive
  /\ Live /\ lease.holder = b
  /\ draft[b] = NoDraft
  /\ e \notin sheet
  /\ \A q \in Bots : draft[q].ed # e
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![b] = [ed |-> e, base |-> sheet]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, acked, lease, alive>>

Write(b) ==
  /\ b \in alive
  /\ Live /\ lease.holder = b
  /\ draft[b] # NoDraft
  /\ sheet' = draft[b].base \cup {draft[b].ed}
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {draft[b].ed}
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![b] = NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, alive>>

Countdown ==
  /\ lease.ttl > 0
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ttl = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, draft, acked, alive>>

GoQuiet(b) ==
  /\ b \in alive
  /\ alive' = alive \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, draft, acked, lease>>

Bin(b) ==
  /\ draft[b] # NoDraft
  /\ (b \notin alive \/ ~Live \/ lease.holder # b)
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![b] = NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, acked, lease, alive>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bots : Take(b) \/ Write(b) \/ GoQuiet(b) \/ Bin(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bots, e \in Edits : Read(b, e)
  \/ Countdown

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost update: every edit the fleet has been told is applied is still on
\* the shared sheet. A write built on a reading taken before somebody else's
\* write would drop that edit right back off again.
AckedNeverLost == acked \subseteq sheet
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Bots = {b1, b2}
  Edits = {e1, e2}
  TTL = 2
  NoBot = nobody
  NoEdit = blank

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AckedNeverLost
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet keeps one shared count sheet for an aisle. The sheet is a plain record of which stock edits have been folded into it, and a bot does not patch the sheet in place -- it reads the whole sheet, keeps that reading, and later writes back the whole thing: exactly what it read, plus its own edit. Write access is granted by a lease with a fixed time to live. The lease is not handed back; it simply runs down, and once it has run out anybody may take a fresh one. That is deliberate, because a bot in this fleet can go quiet without warning and never say anything again, and the fleet has no other way of getting the sheet back from it.

The full action set is: Take -- a bot that is still responding and is carrying no draft takes the sheet lease, but only when no live lease is outstanding, and the fresh lease starts at its full time to live. Read -- the bot holding a live lease, and carrying no draft, picks an edit that is not on the sheet and that no bot is already drafting, and keeps a reading of the whole sheet as it stands together with that edit. Write -- the bot holding a live lease writes its draft back: the sheet becomes exactly the reading it kept plus its own edit, and the fleet is told that edit is applied. Countdown -- time passes and the outstanding lease's remaining life drops by one; when it reaches zero the lease is dead. GoQuiet -- a bot stops responding for good, without announcing it and without giving anything back. Bin -- a draft is thrown away by any bot that has gone quiet or whose lease is no longer live, releasing that edit to be drafted again.

The hazard is a lost update. A bot's reading is a snapshot of the whole sheet, and its write overwrites the whole sheet. If its lease has run out in between, another bot may have taken the lease, read, and written its own edit onto the sheet; a write from the first bot's old reading would then quietly erase that edit even though the fleet had already been told it was applied.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every edit the fleet has been told is applied is still present on the shared count sheet, so no acknowledged update is ever erased by a write built on an out-of-date reading.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p4t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Movers, FloorCap, MaxLoad, Span, Horizon

VARIABLES clock, expiry, spot, load
vars == <<clock, expiry, spot, load>>

\* A staging floor holds only so many pallet places. Admission is by timed
\* lease: a mover is promised places for a span of ticks. Movers here are slow,
\* never broken -- one can still be standing on the floor after its lease has
\* run out, so the admission count has to charge for floor occupancy as well as
\* for live leases, not just for the leases.
RECURSIVE Weigh(_)
Weigh(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
            ELSE LET m == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN load[m] + Weigh(S \ {m})

OnFloor   == {m \in Movers : spot[m] = "floor"}
Committed == {m \in Movers : spot[m] = "floor" \/ expiry[m] > clock}

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
  /\ expiry \in [Movers -> 0 .. (Horizon + Span)]
  /\ spot \in [Movers -> {"yard", "floor", "gone"}]
  /\ load \in [Movers -> 0 .. MaxLoad]

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ expiry = [m \in Movers |-> 0]
  /\ spot = [m \in Movers |-> "yard"]
  /\ load = [m \in Movers |-> 0]

Promise(m, k) ==
  /\ spot[m] = "yard"
  /\ expiry[m] <= clock
  /\ Weigh(Committed) + k <= FloorCap
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![m] = clock + Span]
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![m] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, spot>>

RollOn(m) ==
  /\ spot[m] = "yard"
  /\ load[m] > 0
  /\ expiry[m] > clock
  /\ spot' = [spot EXCEPT ![m] = "floor"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, load>>

Extend(m) ==
  /\ spot[m] = "floor"
  /\ expiry[m] <= clock
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![m] = clock + Span]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, spot, load>>

RollOff(m) ==
  /\ spot[m] = "floor"
  /\ spot' = [spot EXCEPT ![m] = "gone"]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

Tick ==
  /\ clock < Horizon
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, spot, load>>

PromiseStep == \E m \in Movers, k \in 1 .. MaxLoad : Promise(m, k)
OnStep      == \E m \in Movers : RollOn(m)
OffStep     == \E m \in Movers : RollOff(m)

Next == PromiseStep \/ OnStep \/ OffStep
        \/ (\E m \in Movers : Extend(m)) \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(PromiseStep) /\ WF_vars(OnStep) /\ WF_vars(OffStep)

\* Capacity: the pallet places actually occupied on the staging floor never
\* exceed what the floor holds, even while a lapsed lease is still standing on it.
FloorWithinCap == Weigh(OnFloor) <= FloorCap

EveryMoverClears == <>(\A m \in Movers : spot[m] = "gone")
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Movers = {mv1, mv2}
  FloorCap = 2
  MaxLoad = 2
  Span = 2
  Horizon = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT FloorWithinCap
PROPERTY EveryMoverClears
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares one staging floor, and the floor holds only a fixed number of pallet places. Admission to the floor is by timed lease: a mover is promised a number of pallet places for a fixed span of ticks, and the promise simply runs out with the clock rather than being handed back. These movers are slow but never broken -- a mover can still be standing on the floor with its pallets down after its lease has already lapsed, and it will get around to rolling off eventually. That is precisely why the admission count charges for what is physically standing on the floor as well as for what is still under a live lease.

The full action set is: Promise -- a mover waiting in the yard whose lease has lapsed or was never granted is promised a number of pallet places, dated a fixed span ahead of the current clock, but only if those places fit inside the floor's capacity alongside everything already committed, meaning everything standing on the floor plus everything under a live lease. RollOn -- a mover in the yard that has been promised places and whose lease is still live rolls onto the floor. Extend -- a mover already standing on the floor whose lease has lapsed re-dates it a span ahead; it is already being charged for, so this changes nothing about the floor's occupancy. RollOff -- a mover standing on the floor rolls off for good, giving up its places and its lease. Tick -- the clock advances, up to a horizon; this is the only thing that makes a lease lapse.

The trap is to count only the live leases when deciding whether a new promise fits. A slow mover whose lease has lapsed is invisible to that count and yet its pallets are very much still on the floor, so a promise made on the strength of lease bookkeeping alone would put more pallets on the floor than the floor holds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The pallet places actually occupied by movers standing on the staging floor never add up to more than the floor's capacity, even while movers whose leases have lapsed are still standing there.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every mover eventually rolls off the staging floor for good.
