-------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m7p1t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bays, MaxAdd, RateLo, RateHi, MaxWrites

NoJot == [seen |-> -1, tag |-> -1, add |-> 0]
Jots  == {NoJot} \cup [seen : 0 .. RateHi, tag : 0 .. MaxWrites, add : 1 .. MaxAdd]

VARIABLES drum, chain, jot, rated
vars == <<drum, chain, jot, rated>>

\* The shared record is the detergent drum reading. A bay reads the reading
\* together with the length of the write chain, which serves as the version
\* tag, and its write is only accepted if the chain has not grown since.
\* Every accepted write is appended to the chain as a was/now pair.
Tag == Len(chain)

TypeOK ==
  /\ drum \in 0 .. RateHi
  /\ chain \in Seq([was : 0 .. RateHi, now : 0 .. RateHi])
  /\ Len(chain) <= MaxWrites
  /\ jot \in [Bays -> Jots]
  /\ rated \in RateLo .. RateHi

Init ==
  /\ drum = 0
  /\ chain = << >>
  /\ jot = [y \in Bays |-> NoJot]
  /\ rated = RateHi

Sample(y, k) ==
  /\ jot[y] = NoJot
  /\ jot' = [jot EXCEPT ![y] = [seen |-> drum, tag |-> Tag, add |-> k]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drum, chain, rated>>

Swap(y) ==
  /\ jot[y] # NoJot
  /\ jot[y].tag = Tag
  /\ Len(chain) < MaxWrites
  /\ jot[y].seen + jot[y].add <= rated
  /\ drum' = jot[y].seen + jot[y].add
  /\ chain' = Append(chain, [was |-> jot[y].seen, now |-> jot[y].seen + jot[y].add])
  /\ jot' = [jot EXCEPT ![y] = NoJot]
  /\ UNCHANGED rated

Bounce(y) ==
  /\ jot[y] # NoJot
  /\ jot[y].tag # Tag
  /\ jot' = [jot EXCEPT ![y] = NoJot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drum, chain, rated>>

Empty ==
  /\ drum > 0
  /\ Len(chain) < MaxWrites
  /\ chain' = Append(chain, [was |-> drum, now |-> 0])
  /\ drum' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<jot, rated>>

\* The line's throughput rating is re-set while the shift runs, but never below
\* what is already in the drum.
Rerate(v) ==
  /\ v # rated
  /\ v >= drum
  /\ rated' = v
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drum, chain, jot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E y \in Bays, k \in 1 .. MaxAdd : Sample(y, k)
  \/ \E y \in Bays : Swap(y) \/ Bounce(y)
  \/ Empty
  \/ \E v \in RateLo .. RateHi : Rerate(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost update: the write chain is unbroken. It starts from the empty drum,
\* each write picks up exactly where the previous one left off, and the last
\* one is the reading standing now -- so no accepted write was computed from a
\* reading that somebody else had already moved past.
ChainUnbroken ==
  /\ Len(chain) > 0 => chain[1].was = 0
  /\ \A i \in 2 .. Len(chain) : chain[i].was = chain[i - 1].now
  /\ Len(chain) > 0 => chain[Len(chain)].now = drum
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Bays = {y1, y2}
  MaxAdd = 2
  RateLo = 1
  RateHi = 3
  MaxWrites = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ChainUnbroken
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash bays that all top up one shared detergent drum, and the drum's reading is the shared record everybody works from. There is no lock on it. Instead a bay reads the reading and, at the same instant, the length of the drum's write chain, which serves as the version tag. It then comes back later and tries to swap in a new reading. The swap is accepted only if the write chain has not grown in the meantime, which is exactly the compare-and-swap test. Every accepted write is appended to the chain as a was/now pair, so the chain is the complete record of how the reading got to where it is. The line's throughput rating is also re-set while the shift is running.

The full action set is: Sample -- a bay with nothing in hand notes down the drum's current reading, the current chain length as its version tag, and how much it intends to add. Swap -- a bay swaps in its new reading, accepted only if the chain length still equals the tag it noted, if the chain has room, and if the resulting reading stays inside the line's current throughput rating; the was/now pair is appended to the chain. Bounce -- a bay whose noted tag no longer matches the chain length throws its note away without writing. Empty -- the drum is emptied at the tank, which is itself recorded on the chain as a was/now pair from the standing reading down to zero. Rerate -- the line's throughput rating is re-set to a different value while the shift runs, never below what is already standing in the drum.

The hazard is a lost update. A bay's note is a snapshot: between the sample and the swap, another bay may have topped the drum up, or the drum may have been emptied, and either way the reading the first bay is working from is no longer the one on the drum. A write built on that stale reading would silently wipe out whatever happened in between, and the write chain would show it: one link would not pick up where the last one left off.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The drum's write chain is unbroken -- it starts from the empty drum, every link picks up at exactly the reading the previous link left behind, and the last link's result is the reading standing on the drum now, so no accepted write was ever computed from a reading somebody else had already moved past.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m0p6t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Surgeons, Rooms, MaxIssue, Vacant

NoRead == [rm |-> Vacant, ce |-> -1]
Reads  == {NoRead} \cup [rm : Rooms, ce : 0 .. MaxIssue]

VARIABLES issue, booked, stamp, jotting, operated
vars == <<issue, booked, stamp, jotting, operated>>

\* Nobody latches a room. A surgeon reads a room as free together with the
\* issue number of the badge it is holding, then comes back and books, which
\* is refused unless the room is still free and the badge has not been
\* re-issued underneath it. A surgeon here is slow, never absent.
\* Each standing booking is stamped with the badge issue that was presented.
TypeOK ==
  /\ issue \in [Surgeons -> 0 .. MaxIssue]
  /\ booked \in [Rooms -> Surgeons \cup {Vacant}]
  /\ stamp \in [Rooms -> 0 .. MaxIssue]
  /\ jotting \in [Surgeons -> Reads]
  /\ operated \subseteq Surgeons

Init ==
  /\ issue = [g \in Surgeons |-> 0]
  /\ booked = [k \in Rooms |-> Vacant]
  /\ stamp = [k \in Rooms |-> 0]
  /\ jotting = [g \in Surgeons |-> NoRead]
  /\ operated = {}

Study(g, k) ==
  /\ g \notin operated
  /\ jotting[g] = NoRead
  /\ booked[k] = Vacant
  /\ jotting' = [jotting EXCEPT ![g] = [rm |-> k, ce |-> issue[g]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, booked, stamp, operated>>

Book(g) ==
  /\ jotting[g] # NoRead
  /\ booked[jotting[g].rm] = Vacant
  /\ issue[g] = jotting[g].ce
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![jotting[g].rm] = g]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![jotting[g].rm] = jotting[g].ce]
  /\ jotting' = [jotting EXCEPT ![g] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, operated>>

Retry(g) ==
  /\ jotting[g] # NoRead
  /\ \/ booked[jotting[g].rm] # Vacant
     \/ issue[g] # jotting[g].ce
  /\ jotting' = [jotting EXCEPT ![g] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, booked, stamp, operated>>

Operate(g, k) ==
  /\ booked[k] = g
  /\ stamp[k] = issue[g]
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![k] = Vacant]
  /\ operated' = operated \cup {g}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, stamp, jotting>>

\* Re-issuing a badge must also strike every booking that badge is holding,
\* otherwise a room would be standing reserved to an authority nobody holds.
Reissue(g) ==
  /\ issue[g] < MaxIssue
  /\ issue' = [issue EXCEPT ![g] = @ + 1]
  /\ booked' = [k \in Rooms |-> IF booked[k] = g THEN Vacant ELSE booked[k]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, jotting, operated>>

StudyStep   == \E g \in Surgeons, k \in Rooms : Study(g, k)
BookStep    == \E g \in Surgeons : Book(g)
RetryStep   == \E g \in Surgeons : Retry(g)
OperateStep == \E g \in Surgeons, k \in Rooms : Operate(g, k)

Next == StudyStep \/ BookStep \/ RetryStep \/ OperateStep
        \/ \E g \in Surgeons : Reissue(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(StudyStep) /\ WF_vars(BookStep)
        /\ WF_vars(RetryStep) /\ WF_vars(OperateStep)

\* No stale authority: every room standing booked is stamped with exactly the
\* badge issue its holder is carrying now, so no booking rests on a badge that
\* has since been re-issued.
NoStaleBooking ==
  \A k \in Rooms : booked[k] # Vacant => stamp[k] = issue[booked[k]]

EveryoneOperates == <>(\A g \in Surgeons : g \in operated)
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Surgeons = {g1, g2}
  Rooms = {rm1, rm2}
  MaxIssue = 1
  Vacant = empty

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleBooking
PROPERTY EveryoneOperates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler hands rooms to surgeons without any locking at all. A surgeon reads a room off the board as free and, at that same instant, notes the issue number of the badge it is currently carrying. Some time later it comes back and books the room, and the scheduler refuses the booking unless two things are still true: the room is still free, and the surgeon's badge has not been re-issued since the reading. Surgeons here are slow but never absent -- one can take an arbitrarily long time between reading the board and coming back to book, which is exactly when its badge can go out of date underneath it. Every booking standing on the board carries the badge issue that was presented when it was made.

The full action set is: Study -- a surgeon that has not yet operated and is holding no reading picks a room that is free right now and notes it down together with the issue number of its own badge. Book -- a surgeon books the room it noted, accepted only if the room is still free and its badge issue still matches what it noted; the booking is stamped with the badge issue the surgeon presented. Retry -- a surgeon whose noted room has been taken, or whose badge has been re-issued since the reading, throws the reading away and starts over. Operate -- a surgeon whose booking is stamped with the badge issue it is carrying now goes ahead with the surgery and releases the room. Reissue -- a surgeon's badge is re-issued with a new number, and every booking that badge is holding is struck from the board at the same moment.

The hazard is a room standing reserved to an authority nobody actually holds. Because a surgeon can be arbitrarily slow between reading and booking, a badge re-issue can land in that gap. A booking taken on the strength of the old issue number would leave the board showing a reservation backed by credentials that have already been withdrawn, and the surgeon would be operating on authority it no longer has.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every room standing booked on the board is stamped with exactly the badge issue its holding surgeon is carrying at that moment, so no booking or surgery ever rests on a badge that has since been re-issued.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every surgeon eventually gets a room and completes a surgery.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m4p6t4 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Strips, Desks, Windows, DepthLo, DepthHi, NoClr

Clearances == [strip : Strips, by : Desks, win : Windows]

VARIABLES pending, onDuty, depth, inForce
vars == <<pending, onDuty, depth, inForce>>

\* Clearances queue up in one strip-bay of bounded depth; when it is at depth
\* nothing more may be written, which is the backpressure. The depth itself is
\* re-set during the shift as weather and staffing change.
\* A handover replaces the desk on duty for a strip and, in the same motion,
\* pulls that strip's paper -- queued and in force -- because it was written
\* under an authority that no longer exists.
TypeOK ==
  /\ pending \in Seq(Clearances)
  /\ Len(pending) <= DepthHi
  /\ onDuty \in [Strips -> Desks]
  /\ depth \in DepthLo .. DepthHi
  /\ inForce \in [Strips -> Clearances \cup {NoClr}]

Init ==
  /\ pending = << >>
  /\ onDuty = [s \in Strips |-> CHOOSE d \in Desks : TRUE]
  /\ depth = DepthHi
  /\ inForce = [s \in Strips |-> NoClr]

Write(s, w) ==
  /\ Len(pending) < depth
  /\ pending' = Append(pending, [strip |-> s, by |-> onDuty[s], win |-> w])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onDuty, depth, inForce>>

Read ==
  /\ pending # << >>
  /\ inForce[Head(pending).strip] = NoClr
  /\ inForce' = [inForce EXCEPT ![Head(pending).strip] = Head(pending)]
  /\ pending' = Tail(pending)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onDuty, depth>>

Roll(s) ==
  /\ inForce[s] # NoClr
  /\ inForce' = [inForce EXCEPT ![s] = NoClr]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, onDuty, depth>>

Handover(s, d) ==
  /\ onDuty[s] # d
  /\ onDuty' = [onDuty EXCEPT ![s] = d]
  /\ pending' = SelectSeq(pending, LAMBDA c : c.strip # s)
  /\ inForce' = [inForce EXCEPT ![s] = NoClr]
  /\ UNCHANGED depth

Redepth(v) ==
  /\ v # depth
  /\ depth' = v
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, onDuty, inForce>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Strips, w \in Windows : Write(s, w)
  \/ Read
  \/ \E s \in Strips : Roll(s)
  \/ \E s \in Strips, d \in Desks : Handover(s, d)
  \/ \E v \in DepthLo .. DepthHi : Redepth(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale authority anywhere in the system: every clearance still queued in
\* the strip-bay, and every clearance actually in force on a runway, names the
\* desk that is on duty for that strip right now.
NoStaleClearance ==
  /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(pending) : pending[i].by = onDuty[pending[i].strip]
  /\ \A s \in Strips : inForce[s] # NoClr => inForce[s].by = onDuty[s]
=======================================================================
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator works from a single strip-bay: a first-in, first-out queue of written clearances waiting to be read out to aircraft. The strip-bay has a working depth, and while it is at depth no further clearance may be written into it -- that is the backpressure on the writing desks. The depth is not fixed for the shift; it is re-set as weather and staffing change. Each runway strip is worked by exactly one desk at a time, and every clearance written carries the name of the desk that wrote it and the arrival window it grants.

The full action set is: Write -- the desk on duty for a strip writes a new clearance for one arrival window into the back of the strip-bay, allowed only while the strip-bay is under its current working depth. Read -- the clearance at the front of the strip-bay is read out and becomes the clearance in force on its runway, provided that runway has nothing in force already; it leaves the strip-bay. Roll -- the aircraft holding the clearance in force on a runway rolls and the clearance is spent, leaving that runway with nothing in force. Handover -- a strip is handed over to a different desk, and in the same motion every clearance for that strip is pulled: whatever was still queued in the strip-bay is removed, and whatever was in force on that runway is cancelled. Redepth -- the strip-bay's working depth is re-set to a different value during the shift.

The point of the handover pull is authority. A clearance is only as good as the desk that wrote it, and the moment a strip changes hands the outgoing desk's authority for that strip is gone. Paper written under it, whether it is still sitting in the strip-bay or has already been read out to an aircraft, is no longer backed by anybody, and reading out or acting on such a strip would be the allocator taking instruction from a desk that has been relieved.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every clearance still queued in the strip-bay, and every clearance actually in force on a runway, names the desk that is on duty for that strip at that moment, so no relieved desk's paper is ever left standing or acted upon.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m0p2t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Locks, Apps, Vault, Total, MaxVer, MaxPulls, NoLook

Looks == {NoLook} \cup [lk : Locks, v : 0 .. MaxVer]

VARIABLES credits, carried, ver, look, pulls
vars == <<credits, carried, ver, look, pulls>>

\* The home owns a fixed number of guest entry credits and nothing ever mints
\* or burns one -- a credit is only ever moved. A phone app takes a credit off
\* a lock optimistically: it reads the lock's revision, and the take is refused
\* if the revision has moved since. Apps here are slow, never dead: one may sit
\* holding a credit, or holding a reading, for an arbitrarily long time.
RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
               ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
  /\ credits \in [Locks -> 0 .. Total]
  /\ carried \in [Apps -> 0 .. 1]
  /\ ver \in [Locks -> 0 .. MaxVer]
  /\ look \in [Apps -> Looks]
  /\ pulls \in 0 .. MaxPulls

Init ==
  /\ credits = [k \in Locks |-> IF k = Vault THEN Total ELSE 0]
  /\ carried = [a \in Apps |-> 0]
  /\ ver = [k \in Locks |-> 0]
  /\ look = [a \in Apps |-> NoLook]
  /\ pulls = 0

Glance(a, k) ==
  /\ look[a] = NoLook
  /\ carried[a] = 0
  /\ look' = [look EXCEPT ![a] = [lk |-> k, v |-> ver[k]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<credits, carried, ver, pulls>>

Take(a) ==
  /\ look[a] # NoLook
  /\ carried[a] = 0
  /\ ver[look[a].lk] = look[a].v
  /\ ver[look[a].lk] < MaxVer
  /\ credits[look[a].lk] > 0
  /\ pulls < MaxPulls
  /\ credits' = [credits EXCEPT ![look[a].lk] = @ - 1]
  /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![a] = 1]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![look[a].lk] = @ + 1]
  /\ look' = [look EXCEPT ![a] = NoLook]
  /\ pulls' = pulls + 1

Stale(a) ==
  /\ look[a] # NoLook
  /\ ver[look[a].lk] # look[a].v
  /\ look' = [look EXCEPT ![a] = NoLook]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<credits, carried, ver, pulls>>

Fit(a, k) ==
  /\ carried[a] = 1
  /\ ver[k] < MaxVer
  /\ credits' = [credits EXCEPT ![k] = @ + 1]
  /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![a] = 0]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![k] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<look, pulls>>

FitStep == \E a \in Apps, k \in Locks : Fit(a, k)

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Apps, k \in Locks : Glance(a, k) \/ Fit(a, k)
  \/ \E a \in Apps : Take(a) \/ Stale(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(FitStep)

\* Conservation: the credits sitting on the locks plus the credits in apps'
\* hands always add up to what the home owns. Every move is a hand-off.
CreditsConserved == Tally(credits, Locks) + Tally(carried, Apps) = Total

HandsEmptyAgain ==
  (\E a \in Apps : carried[a] = 1) ~> (\A a \in Apps : carried[a] = 0)
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Locks = {lk1, lk2}
  Apps = {ap1, ap2}
  Vault = lk1
  Total = 2
  MaxVer = 4
  MaxPulls = 2
  NoLook = nothing

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CreditsConserved
PROPERTY HandsEmptyAgain
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network shares a fixed number of guest entry credits across its locks. The home owns exactly that many and no more: nothing in the system mints a credit and nothing burns one, so every operation is a hand-off of a credit from one place to another. Phone apps move credits around, and they do it without taking any lock: an app glances at a lock, noting the lock's revision number at that instant, and later tries to take a credit off it. The take is refused if the lock's revision has moved in the meantime, and every credit taken off or fitted onto a lock moves that lock's revision. The apps are slow but never dead: one can sit for an arbitrarily long time holding a stale glance, or holding a credit in hand, and will always eventually get around to fitting it somewhere.

The full action set is: Glance -- an app with empty hands and no reading takes a reading of one lock, noting the lock's current revision number. Fit -- an app carrying a credit fits it onto any lock, which moves that lock's revision; this is the only way a carried credit comes to rest. Take -- an app takes a credit off the lock it glanced at, accepted only if the lock's revision still equals what the app noted, if the lock actually has a credit, and if the home's transfer allowance for the day is not used up; the take moves the lock's revision. Stale -- an app whose noted revision no longer matches the lock's throws the reading away and starts over.

What matters here is not who is allowed to touch which lock. It is that the credits are a conserved quantity: at any instant, some of them are sitting on locks and some are in apps' hands on their way between locks, and those two amounts have to add up to what the home owns. A take that emptied a hand without debiting a lock, or a fit that credited a lock without emptying a hand, would silently change how many guest credits the home has.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The credits sitting on the locks plus the credits carried in apps' hands always add up to exactly the fixed number of guest entry credits the home owns, so no credit is ever created or destroyed in transit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever some app is carrying a credit, every carried credit is eventually fitted back onto a lock, leaving every app's hands empty again.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m4p6t2 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Machines, Desks, QCap

Chits == [mach : Machines, by : Desks]

VARIABLES spool, ledger, ranFrom, busy
vars == <<spool, ledger, ranFrom, busy>>

\* Two regional restock desks run as separate programs but push their chits
\* into one shared spool of bounded depth; a full spool is the backpressure on
\* both of them at once. The ledger says which desk each machine currently
\* answers to, and a machine keeps a note of which desks it has actually run
\* work from since its last re-assignment.
TypeOK ==
  /\ spool \in Seq(Chits)
  /\ Len(spool) <= QCap
  /\ ledger \in [Machines -> Desks]
  /\ ranFrom \in [Machines -> SUBSET Desks]
  /\ busy \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ spool = << >>
  /\ ledger = [m \in Machines |-> CHOOSE d \in Desks : TRUE]
  /\ ranFrom = [m \in Machines |-> {}]
  /\ busy = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]

Push(d, m) ==
  /\ Len(spool) < QCap
  /\ spool' = Append(spool, [mach |-> m, by |-> d])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, ranFrom, busy>>

Run ==
  /\ spool # << >>
  /\ LET c == Head(spool) IN
     /\ ledger[c.mach] = c.by
     /\ ~busy[c.mach]
     /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![c.mach] = TRUE]
     /\ ranFrom' = [ranFrom EXCEPT ![c.mach] = @ \cup {c.by}]
  /\ spool' = Tail(spool)
  /\ UNCHANGED ledger

Refuse ==
  /\ spool # << >>
  /\ ledger[Head(spool).mach] # Head(spool).by
  /\ spool' = Tail(spool)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, ranFrom, busy>>

Finish(m) ==
  /\ busy[m]
  /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, ledger, ranFrom>>

\* Re-assignment happens only while the machine is idle, and it wipes the
\* machine's note, because from that moment the old desk has no standing here.
Reassign(m, d) ==
  /\ ledger[m] # d
  /\ ~busy[m]
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![m] = d]
  /\ ranFrom' = [ranFrom EXCEPT ![m] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, busy>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Desks, m \in Machines : Push(d, m) \/ Reassign(m, d)
  \/ Run
  \/ Refuse
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Finish(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized or stale desk gets to drive a machine: every desk a machine
\* has actually run work from since its last re-assignment is the one desk the
\* ledger says it answers to.
OnlyBoundDeskRan == \A m \in Machines : ranFrom[m] \subseteq {ledger[m]}
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Machines = {mv1, mv2}
  Desks = {north, south}
  QCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyBoundDeskRan
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked from two regional desks. The two desks run as completely separate programs -- neither can see the other's plans -- but they do not have separate work queues: they push their restock chits into one shared spool of bounded depth, first in and first out. When the spool is at depth neither desk can push anything, and that shared cap is the backpressure on both of them at once. A central ledger records, for each machine, the one desk that machine currently answers to, and machines can be re-assigned from one desk to the other. Each machine also keeps a note of which desks it has actually run work from since it was last re-assigned.

The full action set is: Push -- a desk appends a chit naming a machine into the shared spool, allowed only while the spool is under its depth cap; a desk may push a chit for any machine, including one it does not currently own. Run -- the chit at the front of the spool is taken off and run, but only if the ledger says that machine answers to the desk that wrote the chit and the machine is not already busy; running it adds that desk to the machine's note. Refuse -- the chit at the front of the spool names a desk the machine no longer answers to, so it is discarded unrun. Finish -- a busy machine completes its restock and goes idle. Reassign -- a machine that is idle is re-assigned in the ledger to the other desk, and its note is wiped, because from that moment the previous desk has no standing at that machine at all.

The hazard comes from the shared spool. A chit written by one desk can be sitting in the spool while the ledger is re-assigned underneath it, and because neither desk can see the other, the desk that wrote it has no way of knowing its authority for that machine is gone. The only thing standing between a relieved desk and a machine acting on its instructions is the check made at the moment the chit reaches the front.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every machine, every desk it has actually run work from since its last re-assignment is exactly the desk the ledger says it answers to, so no machine has ever acted on a chit from a desk that did not own it.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m7p4t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Items, Cap, MaxTag, MaxDrafts

Slips == [item : Items, seen : 0 .. Cap, tg : 0 .. MaxTag]

VARIABLES filled, tag, wire, batch, drafts
vars == <<filled, tag, wire, batch, drafts>>

\* The batch's fill level lives in one compare-and-swap register: a fill count
\* and a tag that moves on every accepted write. A clerk copies the pair onto a
\* slip and posts it; slips travel over an unordered wire and are picked up in
\* any order at all, so a slip can be acted on long after its pair went stale.
Fits(s) == s.tg = tag /\ s.seen + 1 <= Cap /\ tag < MaxTag

TypeOK ==
  /\ filled \in 0 .. Cap
  /\ tag \in 0 .. MaxTag
  /\ wire \subseteq Slips
  /\ batch \subseteq Items
  /\ drafts \in 0 .. MaxDrafts

Init ==
  /\ filled = 0
  /\ tag = 0
  /\ wire = {}
  /\ batch = {}
  /\ drafts = 0

Draft(i) ==
  /\ drafts < MaxDrafts
  /\ i \notin batch
  /\ \A s \in wire : s.item # i
  /\ wire' = wire \cup {[item |-> i, seen |-> filled, tg |-> tag]}
  /\ drafts' = drafts + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<filled, tag, batch>>

Swap(s) ==
  /\ s \in wire
  /\ Fits(s)
  /\ filled' = s.seen + 1
  /\ tag' = tag + 1
  /\ batch' = batch \cup {s.item}
  /\ wire' = wire \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED drafts

Bounce(s) ==
  /\ s \in wire
  /\ ~Fits(s)
  /\ wire' = wire \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<filled, tag, batch, drafts>>

Pull(i) ==
  /\ i \in batch
  /\ filled > 0
  /\ tag < MaxTag
  /\ batch' = batch \ {i}
  /\ filled' = filled - 1
  /\ tag' = tag + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wire, drafts>>

SwapStep   == \E s \in Slips : Swap(s)
BounceStep == \E s \in Slips : Bounce(s)

Next == (\E i \in Items : Draft(i) \/ Pull(i)) \/ SwapStep \/ BounceStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(SwapStep) /\ WF_vars(BounceStep)

\* Capacity: the settlement batch never carries more instructions than it is
\* rated for. The register is the only admission control, so a write accepted
\* on a fill count somebody else had already moved past would let extra
\* instructions in behind it.
BatchWithinCap == Cardinality(batch) <= Cap

WireClears == (wire # {}) ~> (wire = {})
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Items = {i1, i2, i3}
  Cap = 2
  MaxTag = 3
  MaxDrafts = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BatchWithinCap
PROPERTY WireClears
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is rated to carry only so many instructions at once. The whole of that admission control lives in one compare-and-swap register holding two things: how full the batch currently is, and a tag that moves every time the register is written. A clerk who wants to add an instruction copies the pair -- the fill count and the tag -- onto a slip and posts the slip. Slips travel over an unordered wire and are picked up in whatever order they happen to be picked up in, so a slip can be acted on long after the pair it was copied from stopped being true.

The full action set is: Draft -- a clerk copies the register's current fill count and tag onto a slip for an instruction that is not in the batch and has no slip already out, and posts it onto the wire; the shift's drafting allowance limits how many slips can ever be posted. Swap -- a slip is picked off the wire and the register is written from it: this is accepted only if the tag on the slip still equals the register's tag, if one more instruction still fits inside the rating, and if the register has tag movements left; on acceptance the fill count becomes the slip's count plus one, the tag moves, and the instruction joins the batch. Bounce -- a slip that fails any part of that test is picked off the wire and torn up without touching the register. Pull -- an instruction is pulled back out of the batch, which drops the fill count by one and moves the tag.

The hazard is that a slip is a snapshot of the admission control, not the admission control itself. Several clerks can copy the very same fill count, and because the wire is unordered they can come back in any sequence. If the tag test were not there, each of them would write a fill count computed from the same starting point, the register would end up claiming the batch is far emptier than it is, and instruction after instruction would be admitted behind the batch's rating.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of instructions carried in the settlement batch never exceeds the rating the batch is admitted for.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever slips are out on the wire, every one of them is eventually picked up and either swapped in or torn up, so the wire always clears.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m9p3t1 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Lines, Faces, MaxPlan, BagCap, NoFace, NoLine

Orders == [line : Lines, face : Faces, plan : 0 .. MaxPlan]

VARIABLES plan, sits, fills, bag
vars == <<plan, sits, fills, bag>>

\* Two books are kept: which face each product line sits in, and which line
\* fills each face. They are meant to be exact inverses of each other.
\* Planogram orders travel in an unordered bag and are picked out in any order,
\* so an order stamped with a superseded plan number can surface at any time.
TypeOK ==
  /\ plan \in 0 .. MaxPlan
  /\ sits \in [Lines -> Faces \cup {NoFace}]
  /\ fills \in [Faces -> Lines \cup {NoLine}]
  /\ bag \subseteq Orders
  /\ Cardinality(bag) <= BagCap

Init ==
  /\ plan = 0
  /\ sits = [l \in Lines |-> NoFace]
  /\ fills = [f \in Faces |-> NoLine]
  /\ bag = {}

Cut(l, f) ==
  /\ Cardinality(bag) < BagCap
  /\ bag' = bag \cup {[line |-> l, face |-> f, plan |-> plan]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, sits, fills>>

Post(o) ==
  /\ o \in bag
  /\ o.plan = plan
  /\ sits[o.line] = NoFace
  /\ fills[o.face] = NoLine
  /\ sits' = [sits EXCEPT ![o.line] = o.face]
  /\ fills' = [fills EXCEPT ![o.face] = o.line]
  /\ bag' = bag \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED plan

Shred(o) ==
  /\ o \in bag
  /\ \/ o.plan # plan
     \/ sits[o.line] # NoFace
     \/ fills[o.face] # NoLine
  /\ bag' = bag \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, sits, fills>>

Strike(l) ==
  /\ sits[l] # NoFace
  /\ fills' = [fills EXCEPT ![sits[l]] = NoLine]
  /\ sits' = [sits EXCEPT ![l] = NoFace]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, bag>>

\* A new planogram epoch wipes both books at once; every order still in the
\* bag from the old epoch becomes worthless the moment the number moves.
Replan ==
  /\ plan < MaxPlan
  /\ plan' = plan + 1
  /\ sits' = [l \in Lines |-> NoFace]
  /\ fills' = [f \in Faces |-> NoLine]
  /\ UNCHANGED bag

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Lines, f \in Faces : Cut(l, f)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Post(o) \/ Shred(o)
  \/ \E l \in Lines : Strike(l)
  \/ Replan

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: the two books are exact inverses. If a face were ever
\* handed to a second product line, the first line's entry would still name
\* that face while the face's entry named somebody else.
BooksAreInverses ==
  /\ \A l \in Lines : sits[l] # NoFace => fills[sits[l]] = l
  /\ \A f \in Faces : fills[f] # NoLine => sits[fills[f]] = f
=======================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Lines = {pa, pb}
  Faces = {sl1, sl2}
  MaxPlan = 1
  BagCap = 2
  NoFace = unplaced
  NoLine = empty

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BooksAreInverses
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network keeps a planogram: which shelf face each product line occupies. Head office keeps two books that are meant to be exact mirrors of one another -- one says which face a product line sits in, the other says which product line fills a face. Placement orders are cut by the planners and travel to the machines in an unordered bag, so orders are picked out and acted on in whatever order they come to hand, not the order they were cut. Every order is stamped with the planogram number that was current when it was cut, and the whole planogram is periodically re-cut under a new number.

The full action set is: Cut -- the planners cut an order naming a product line and a shelf face, stamped with the current planogram number, and drop it in the bag, which they can only do while the bag is under its capacity. Post -- an order is picked out of the bag and posted into both books at once, but only if its planogram number is still current, the product line is not already placed, and the face is not already filled. Shred -- an order is picked out of the bag and shredded unposted, because its planogram number has been superseded, or because its line has already been placed, or because its face has already been filled. Strike -- a placed product line is struck from both books together, freeing its face. Replan -- a new planogram number is issued and both books are wiped clean at once, which makes every order still sitting in the bag worthless.

The hazard is double allocation of one shelf face. Because the bag is unordered, two orders naming the same face can be picked out at any distance apart in time, and an order cut under an old planogram can surface long after the machines have moved on. If a second line were ever posted into a face that was already filled, the two books would fall out of step with each other: the first line's entry would still name that face while the face's entry named the newcomer.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The two planogram books are exact inverses of each other -- every placed product line's face names that line back, and every filled face's line names that face back -- so no shelf face is ever allocated to two product lines.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m1p0t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS DeskCount, MaxEdit, MaxRev

Desks == 1 .. DeskCount
Nxt(d) == (d % DeskCount) + 1

VARIABLES baton, phase, todo, rev
vars == <<baton, phase, todo, rev>>

\* The opening auction's order book may be amended by one desk at a time. The
\* right to amend travels the ring as a single baton. A desk that wants the
\* book keeps the baton until it has worked through all of its amendments --
\* desks here are slow, never absent, so it always finishes and lets go.
Holders == {d \in Desks : baton[d]}

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in [Desks -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ phase \in [Desks -> {"quiet", "queued", "amending", "done"}]
  /\ todo \in [Desks -> 0 .. MaxEdit]
  /\ rev \in 0 .. MaxRev

Init ==
  /\ baton = [d \in Desks |-> d = 1]
  /\ phase = [d \in Desks |-> "quiet"]
  /\ todo = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
  /\ rev = 0

Wake(d, k) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "quiet"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "queued"]
  /\ todo' = [todo EXCEPT ![d] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, rev>>

Grab(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "queued"
  /\ baton[d]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "amending"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, todo, rev>>

Edit(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "amending"
  /\ todo[d] > 0
  /\ rev < MaxRev
  /\ rev' = rev + 1
  /\ todo' = [todo EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, phase>>

Yield(d) ==
  /\ phase[d] = "amending"
  /\ todo[d] = 0
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, todo, rev>>

\* The baton is handed on, never copied: it leaves one desk in the same step
\* it arrives at the next. A desk that is queued or amending holds on to it.
Hand(d) ==
  /\ baton[d]
  /\ phase[d] \in {"quiet", "done"}
  /\ baton' = [baton EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE, ![Nxt(d)] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, todo, rev>>

WakeStep  == \E d \in Desks, k \in 1 .. MaxEdit : Wake(d, k)
GrabStep  == \E d \in Desks : Grab(d)
EditStep  == \E d \in Desks : Edit(d)
YieldStep == \E d \in Desks : Yield(d)
HandStep  == \E d \in Desks : Hand(d)

Next == WakeStep \/ GrabStep \/ EditStep \/ YieldStep \/ HandStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(WakeStep) /\ WF_vars(GrabStep) /\ WF_vars(EditStep)
        /\ WF_vars(YieldStep) /\ WF_vars(HandStep)

\* Mutual exclusion: there is exactly one baton in the ring at all times, and
\* only a desk holding it is ever inside the order book.
BatonRulesTheBook ==
  /\ Cardinality(Holders) = 1
  /\ \A d \in Desks : phase[d] = "amending" => baton[d]

EveryDeskFinishes == <>(\A d \in Desks : phase[d] = "done")
========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  DeskCount = 3
  MaxEdit = 2
  MaxRev = 6

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BatonRulesTheBook
PROPERTY EveryDeskFinishes
nl:
In a stock exchange's opening auction the order book is the critical resource: only one trading desk may be inside it amending orders at any instant. The desks sit in a ring, and the right to amend travels around that ring as a single baton, handed from each desk to the next one downstream. A desk that has amendments to make keeps the baton until it has worked through all of them. These desks are slow but never absent: one can take an arbitrarily long time inside the book, and the ring simply waits, but it always finishes and always lets go.

The full action set is: Wake -- a quiet desk decides it has some number of amendments to make and joins the queue for the book. Grab -- a queued desk that is holding the baton goes inside the order book and starts amending. Edit -- a desk inside the book makes one amendment, which moves the book's revision on by one and leaves it one fewer to do. Yield -- a desk inside the book that has no amendments left comes out and is finished for the session. Hand -- a desk holding the baton hands it to the next desk downstream on the ring; the baton leaves the one desk in the very same step it arrives at the next, and a desk that is queued or amending will not hand it on.

The whole exclusion argument rests on the baton being singular. It is handed on, never copied and never duplicated: at every instant exactly one desk in the ring has it. Because being inside the book requires holding it, two desks can never be inside the book at once -- there is simply not enough baton to go around.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every instant exactly one desk in the ring holds the baton, and any desk that is inside the order book amending is a desk holding it, so two desks can never be amending the order book at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every desk eventually gets the baton, makes all of its amendments and finishes for the session.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m5p6t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Orders, Wardens

VARIABLES signers, standing, answering, spent
vars == <<signers, standing, answering, spent>>

\* Every shed order has to be countersigned by a majority of the substation
\* wardens before it stands. A warden can stop answering at any moment without
\* saying so; its signature is then worth nothing, and orders resting on it are
\* pulled at once rather than being left standing on dead authority.
Enough(o) == 2 * Cardinality(signers[o]) > Cardinality(Wardens)

TypeOK ==
  /\ signers \in [Orders -> SUBSET Wardens]
  /\ standing \subseteq Orders
  /\ answering \subseteq Wardens
  /\ spent \subseteq Orders

Init ==
  /\ signers = [o \in Orders |-> {}]
  /\ standing = {}
  /\ answering = Wardens
  /\ spent = {}

Sign(w, o) ==
  /\ w \in answering
  /\ o \notin standing
  /\ o \notin spent
  /\ w \notin signers[o]
  /\ signers' = [signers EXCEPT ![o] = @ \cup {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, answering, spent>>

Unsign(w, o) ==
  /\ w \in answering
  /\ o \notin standing
  /\ w \in signers[o]
  /\ signers' = [signers EXCEPT ![o] = @ \ {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, answering, spent>>

Raise(o) ==
  /\ o \notin standing
  /\ o \notin spent
  /\ signers[o] \subseteq answering
  /\ Enough(o)
  /\ standing' = standing \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<signers, answering, spent>>

\* A warden going quiet pulls every standing order it had countersigned.
GoQuiet(w) ==
  /\ w \in answering
  /\ answering' = answering \ {w}
  /\ standing' = standing \ {o \in Orders : w \in signers[o]}
  /\ spent' = spent \cup {o \in standing : w \in signers[o]}
  /\ UNCHANGED signers

Shed(o) ==
  /\ o \in standing
  /\ standing' = standing \ {o}
  /\ spent' = spent \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<signers, answering>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Wardens, o \in Orders : Sign(w, o) \/ Unsign(w, o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Raise(o) \/ Shed(o)
  \/ \E w \in Wardens : GoQuiet(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No order rests on absent or withdrawn authority: every standing shed order
\* is countersigned only by wardens that are answering right now, and by enough
\* of them to make a majority of the whole board.
StandingOrdersAuthorised ==
  \A o \in Orders :
    o \in standing => (signers[o] \subseteq answering /\ Enough(o))
========================================================================
nl:
A power-grid load shedder never drops a feeder on one person's say-so. A shed order has to be countersigned by a majority of the substation wardens before it stands, and only a standing order is ever acted on. The wardens are not reliable: one can stop answering at any moment, silently, with no announcement and no chance to hand anything over. From the instant a warden stops answering its countersignature is worth nothing, and the shedder is built to pull orders that were resting on it rather than leave them standing on authority that no longer exists.

The full action set is: Sign -- a warden that is still answering countersigns an order that is not yet standing and not yet spent. Unsign -- a warden that is still answering takes its countersignature back off an order that has not yet been raised. Raise -- an order is raised to standing, which requires that every countersignature on it belongs to a warden answering right now and that those signatures make up a strict majority of the whole warden board. GoQuiet -- a warden stops answering without warning; every standing order carrying its countersignature is pulled down and marked spent in the same motion. Shed -- a standing order is acted on, the feeder is dropped, and the order is marked spent.

The hazard is the shedder acting on authority nobody is behind any more. A silent failure is invisible by construction: the warden simply stops, and its signature sits there on the paperwork looking exactly like a live one. If a standing order were allowed to keep resting on signatures from wardens that had gone quiet, the shedder would be dropping load on the word of participants that are no longer part of the board at all -- and a bare majority is precisely the margin where losing one warden matters.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every shed order that is standing is countersigned only by wardens that are answering at that moment, and by a strict majority of the whole warden board, so no order ever rests on a silent or withdrawn signature.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m2p1t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS WardDesk, DepotDesk, Fridges, NoReq

Reqs == WardDesk \cup DepotDesk

VARIABLES sheet, step, held, image
vars == <<sheet, step, held, image>>

\* Two desks track the same blood-bank pool independently and both amend one
\* shared count sheet. A requisition runs two-phase commit: it must hold every
\* fridge before it may take its reading of the sheet, and its write replaces
\* the sheet with that reading plus itself.
AllHeld(r) == \A f \in Fridges : held[f] = r

TypeOK ==
  /\ sheet \subseteq Reqs
  /\ step \in [Reqs -> {"fresh", "gathering", "readied", "posted", "torn"}]
  /\ held \in [Fridges -> Reqs \cup {NoReq}]
  /\ image \in [Reqs -> SUBSET Reqs]

Init ==
  /\ sheet = {}
  /\ step = [r \in Reqs |-> "fresh"]
  /\ held = [f \in Fridges |-> NoReq]
  /\ image = [r \in Reqs |-> {}]

Open(r) ==
  /\ step[r] = "fresh"
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "gathering"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, held, image>>

Prepare(r, f) ==
  /\ step[r] = "gathering"
  /\ held[f] = NoReq
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![f] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, step, image>>

\* The reading is only taken once every fridge is held, which is what stops a
\* second requisition from moving the sheet underneath this one.
Take(r) ==
  /\ step[r] = "gathering"
  /\ AllHeld(r)
  /\ image' = [image EXCEPT ![r] = sheet]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "readied"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, held>>

Post(r) ==
  /\ step[r] = "readied"
  /\ AllHeld(r)
  /\ sheet' = image[r] \cup {r}
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "posted"]
  /\ held' = [f \in Fridges |-> IF held[f] = r THEN NoReq ELSE held[f]]
  /\ UNCHANGED image

Tear(r) ==
  /\ step[r] = "gathering"
  /\ \E f \in Fridges : held[f] \notin {NoReq, r}
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "torn"]
  /\ held' = [f \in Fridges |-> IF held[f] = r THEN NoReq ELSE held[f]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, image>>

OpenStep    == \E r \in Reqs : Open(r)
PrepareStep == \E r \in Reqs, f \in Fridges : Prepare(r, f)
TakeStep    == \E r \in Reqs : Take(r)
PostStep    == \E r \in Reqs : Post(r)
TearStep    == \E r \in Reqs : Tear(r)

Next == OpenStep \/ PrepareStep \/ TakeStep \/ PostStep \/ TearStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(OpenStep) /\ WF_vars(PrepareStep) /\ WF_vars(TakeStep)
        /\ WF_vars(PostStep) /\ WF_vars(TearStep)

\* No lost update: the shared sheet carries exactly the requisitions the desks
\* have been told were posted -- no more, and crucially no fewer, so no posted
\* requisition is ever erased by a write built on an older reading.
SheetMatchesPostings ==
  \A r \in Reqs : (step[r] = "posted") <=> (r \in sheet)

EveryReqDecided ==
  <>(\A r \in Reqs : step[r] \in {"posted", "torn"})
========================================================================
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker runs as two separate desks: a ward-side desk and a depot-side desk. They are independent programs that cannot see each other's work, but they track one shared pool of units and both amend one shared count sheet. The sheet is not patched in place: a requisition reads the whole sheet, keeps that reading, and writes the sheet back as exactly that reading plus itself. Because of that, every requisition runs as a two-phase commit across the fridges: it must be holding every fridge in the bank before it is allowed to take its reading, and it still has to be holding them all when it writes.

The full action set is: Open -- a fresh requisition from either desk starts gathering fridges. Prepare -- a gathering requisition takes hold of one fridge that is currently free. Take -- a gathering requisition that is holding every fridge in the bank takes its reading of the whole count sheet and is readied. Post -- a readied requisition that is still holding every fridge writes the sheet back as its reading plus itself, is recorded as posted, and lets all its fridges go. Tear -- a gathering requisition that finds some fridge already held by a different requisition tears itself up and lets go of whatever fridges it had taken.

The hazard is a lost update, and the two independent desks make it easy to reach. A reading is a snapshot of the whole sheet and a write replaces the whole sheet, so if a requisition could take its reading before it had every fridge, the other desk's requisition could post in between and the first one's write would silently erase it. Unanimous holding across the fridges is the only thing that makes the reading and the write behave as one indivisible step.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared count sheet carries exactly the requisitions the desks have been told were posted, no more and no fewer, so no posted requisition is ever erased from the sheet by a write built on an older reading.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every requisition eventually reaches a decision, either posted to the sheet or torn up.
